Smoke and promotion are separate on purpose. `staging-smoke.yml` runs on every push to master, polls `/api/v1/public/build` and `/build.json` until both equal `github.sha` (15-minute deadline; the probe yields an empty string for a service that is down, 404s or predates the field, so an unidentifiable build never matches), runs `e2e/tests/smoke.spec.ts` against staging and reports — it never promotes. `nightly-promote.yml` is the one that would promote, runs at 03:00 UTC, and stays a no-op until `STAGING_BASE_URL` arms it; it now applies the same commit gate in place of its former "the API answered 401" check, which could not tell the commit under test from a stale build. The two read different repository variables (`STAGING_URL` vs `STAGING_BASE_URL`) so that smoke-testing staging cannot arm automatic promotion by accident, which keeps promotion the human decision `CLAUDE.md` requires.

The smoke journey signs in as a pre-provisioned account when `SMOKE_EMAIL` and `SMOKE_PASSWORD` are set and registers a throwaway user when they are not, so a closed staging and CI's open compose stack both work; it reads the account's display name from `GET /api/v1/auth/me`, because a later step asserts who captured a baseline and on that path the deployment owns the name. `OPENV_NOINDEX` makes `docker-entrypoint.d/45-openv-noindex.sh` write an `X-Robots-Tag: noindex, nofollow, noarchive` into `/etc/nginx/openv/noindex.conf`, included from `security-headers.conf` so it survives every location that adds a header of its own — a header rather than a `robots.txt` Disallow, which would stop the crawl that reads the noindex.

Compatibility: `internal/api/route_inventory_test.go` walks the router and compares `METHOD PATH` lines with `internal/api/testdata/routes.txt`; a missing route fails with the deprecation rule quoted, an added route fails until the file is regenerated (`UPDATE_ROUTES=1 go test ./internal/api -run TestRouteInventory`), so the HTTP surface cannot shrink by accident.

artifacts.title: Project hierarchy, refines link, both-end link visibility and verification flow-up
artifacts.body:
Built (REQ-144, REQ-145, REQ-146; DSC-8). Migration 0038 adds `projects.parent_project_id` (nullable, `ON DELETE SET NULL`, indexed). `projects.Project.ParentProjectID`; `UpdateProjectRequest.ParentProjectID` is tri-state (nil unchanged, "" detach, id attach) and the service refuses a missing parent, one in another workspace, the project itself or a descendant (`ErrParent*`, answered 400); `Ancestors` walks the chain with a loop guard; `ListChildren` and `GET /api/v1/projects/{id}/children` list the children.

`links.TypeRefines` ("refines", requirement → requirement) joins the rule table; `LinkRepository.FindAll` joins both endpoints (`fa.project_id = $1 OR ta.project_id = $1`), so a link touching a project from either end is in its link list, export, baseline, coverage, matrix and AI map. `CreateLink` keeps editor rights on both ends for a cross-project link except `refines`, which needs viewer rights on the target's project. `exports.ProjectExport.LinkedArtifacts` (`resolveLinked`: the far end of every link whose endpoint is not local, with project name, ref, type, title, status; `QualifiedRef` renders "Landing gear / REQ-12") is embedded in every export and served by `GET /api/v1/projects/{id}/linked-artifacts`; `exports.Apply` keeps a link to a foreign endpoint when its local end survives.

Flow-up: `vv.CoverageEntry` gains `Refinements` (each refiner's id, project, ref, title and its own rollup), `FlowDown` and `ViaRefinements`. `vv.RefinersByRequirement` reads the `refines` links whose target is local and whose source is a linked requirement; `ChildProjectIDs` names the projects to read; `ApplyFlowDown` merges by severity (fail 4, blocked 3, unrun 2, uncovered/method-missing 1, pass 0): no own evidence takes the flow-down and sets `ViaRefinements`, own evidence keeps the worse, method-missing stays. `Handler.coverageWithFlowDown` computes each child project's live coverage the same way (recursively, with a seen set) and feeds the rollups in; `GetCoverage` and `GetGaps` use it, and `GapAnalysis` no longer lists a requirement with refinements as lacking a test case.

Frontend: Project settings → General shows the parent picker (candidates exclude the project and its descendants) and the child projects; the artifact editor's link panel offers the parent project's requirements as `refines` targets, labelled with the parent's name; cross-project endpoints are titled from `linked-artifacts` in the editor and the details view; the V&V dashboard shows each requirement's refinements with their rollups and says when the rollup came from them. Gated by feature key `flow-down` (0.3.0): the parent write, `refines` links and the parties write answer 403 with a pointer to workspace settings on a stable-channel workspace that has not received it.

artifacts.title: Artifact owners, reference parties and owner-filtered downloads
artifacts.body:
Built (REQ-147, REQ-148; DSC-8). The owner is the `owner` attribute: `exports.FieldOwner` joins `StandardFields` (a project's own definition of the key keeps its label), `exports.OwnerOf` reads it trimmed, and migration 0038 adds an expression index on `(project_id, attributes->>'owner')` for live rows. `GET /api/v1/artifacts` takes `owner=` (exact match) through `ListArtifactsPage(projectID, type, owner, limit, offset)` and the repository's page and count queries; the MCP `list_artifacts` tool takes `owner`.

Reference parties live in the project's settings JSON under `parties` (`settings.Party{Name, Note, Default}`, `PartiesFromSettings`, `ValidateParties`: trimmed, non-empty, unique case-insensitively, at most 100, the default never stored; `WithDefault` puts the workspace's name first and marked default, keeping a note stored under the same name). `GET /api/v1/projects/{id}/parties` answers the effective list (viewer), `PUT` replaces the project's own (editor, 400 on `ErrInvalidParties`).

Downloads: `exports.Selection.Owners` (comma-separated `owners=` on every `/download/{format}`), applied in `exports.Apply` beside sections and types (headings stay with `IncludeHeadings`; a link to a foreign endpoint survives with its local end); `exports.Owners` counts the owners present, most artifacts first, served as `owners` in `/download/options`. The wizard's Content step lists them under Owners, nothing ticked meaning everyone; `downloadSelection` carries `owners` on the form, the wire and the query, and the summary reads "owned by …". `scripts/openv/sync.py export` gains `--owner` (repeatable), `--types`, `--no-headings` and `--format` for every download format, reading binary formats raw.

Frontend: the artifact editor's Owner field suggests the project's parties and members (any name accepted); the artifact header shows the owner as a chip; the module view's filter panel offers Owner with the values present; Project settings → General lists the parties with add and remove, the workspace's own marked and fixed. Gated by feature key `artifact-owners` (0.3.0).

artifacts.title: Share links, the reviewer role, social preview cards and the open-source showcase
artifacts.body: `internal/domain/sharelinks` mints links (random token, SHA-256 hash stored in `project_share_links`, migration 0039) with a role of `public` or `reviewer`, a label, an optional expiry and a revocation time; `Resolve` answers one error for every unusable token. `members.RoleReviewer` sits between viewer and editor in the role ladder; `POST /chatter` requires it, every other write keeps its editor gate. `internal/api/share_handlers.go` registers the owner-gated `/projects/{id}/share-links` and `/share-links/{id}` routes, the open `/api/v1/public/share/{token}` family (JSON with the live export for a public link; an HTML page carrying Open Graph and Twitter-card tags plus a refresh into the app; a 1200×630 PNG card drawn with the Go fonts in `share_preview.go`), `POST /auth/share/accept` (session cookie only, grants reviewer unless a stronger role is held) and the `/api/v1/public/open-source/projects` listing and snapshot endpoints, which take every project of an `open_source`-plan workspace with a baseline. Lookups share the invite-preview rate limiter; `requestlog.go` redacts share tokens. The frontend's nginx sends `/share/<token>` and `/open-source/p/<id>` to the API page so unfurlers read the tags; `SharedProjectView` renders the snapshot without a session at `/s/:token`, `/share/:token` and `/open-source/:id`; Project settings → Access mints and revokes links, gated on feature key `share-links` (0.4.0); Login takes `?share=` up after sign-in.

artifacts.title: Storefront shell, site pages, demo videos and the description row in documents
artifacts.body:
`frontend/src/site/SiteShell.tsx` is the storefront frame (header with the site navigation, footer, section and card blocks) shared by the landing page and the new pages in `frontend/src/site/`: How it works (inline SVG diagrams of the artifact graph, the agent loop, the deployment and the three access levels), Demos (five `<video>` elements served from `public/videos`, recorded with Playwright on the platform's own project and narrated with a synthesised voice, two on an iPhone viewport), FAQ (`<details>` groups: security on every tier, what each tier gets, sharing and review, practical), Open-source projects (the public listing), Customer stories and White papers (placeholders that say so). Copy lives in `site/content.ts` and `landing/content.ts`; every route is in the public-path allowlist.

`internal/domain/reports/report.go` adds a Description row to the fields table carrying the artifact body's parsed blocks (`fieldRow.Blocks`). The Word renderer (`cellBlocks`) lays the blocks out inside the cell through the ordinary block renderer, so hyperlinks, list numbering and code styles are registered as usual, and leaves the row free to break across pages. The PDF renderer (`blocksRow`) draws the blocks in the value column with the content width inset for the cell padding, then revisits every page the row covered (`SetPage`) to draw the label cell and borders. Neither renderer flows the body below the table any more: the description row is the statement's only copy in a tabled artifact's section. Headings and description artifacts, which have no table, still flow as prose.

artifacts.title: Plan endpoint for platform admins
artifacts.body: `PUT /api/v1/orgs/{id}/plan` in `internal/api/org_handlers.go` checks `users.IsAdmin` and calls `orgs.Service.SetPlan`, which validates the name with `orgs.ValidPlan` (the tiers, `self_host`, `open_source` and the legacy aliases), writes only the `plan` column through `Repository.SetPlan`, and re-resolves the release channel. Errors map to 400 (unknown plan), 404 (unknown workspace) and 403/401 for everyone who is not a platform admin. `scripts/openv/sync.py api PUT ...` reaches it with an admin sign-in.

artifacts.title: Project outline and project-mode cards for the V&V Assistant
artifacts.body:
Built (REQ-49, gated under REQ-137). Beside the project the assistant used to see an empty wizard state and a prompt that ended "Do not create or modify OpenV artifacts yourself", so it could neither name what to change nor propose a change; and the only shapes it had were the wizard's six, which the notes panel filed as drafts under the standard headings. Beside the wizard it saw only the form, so a resumed definition — which sits on top of artifacts that already exist — could not touch them.

**Backend.** Every turn (`launchGuidedTurn`) lists the project's artifacts and passes a `projectOutline{Artifacts, Edits}` to `buildGuidedCopilotPrompt`. `internal/api/guided_project_outline.go` renders one line per artifact — reference, type, title — indented under its parent in sort order (a stale parent pointer promotes its children rather than losing them; a cycle guard stops descent), cut at `outlineBudget` (24k characters) in document order with a count of what was left out. The outline is fenced `<<<PROJECT_OUTLINE … PROJECT_OUTLINE>>>` after the trust rules, since titles are written by whoever can edit the project. Beside the wizard it follows the `WIZARD_STATE` block, whose legend now says that an entry carrying `artifact_id` is already an artifact (the green dot) to be changed with an edit or move card naming that id or its reference, never `replaces`; beside the project it replaces the state block. The outline legend names the project id and tells the assistant, which carries `mcp__openv__*`, to read an artifact in full with `get_artifact` before proposing a change to its text, and to use `get_project_tree`, `search_artifacts` and `list_links_for_artifact` for more. `projectChangeRules(edits, inWizard)` adds the response rules in both modes: with the gate on, `{"kind":"artifact", type, title, body, attributes, parent, after}`, `{"kind":"edit", ref, title?, body?, attributes?}` and `{"kind":"move", ref, parent?, before|after|position}`, an artifact nameable by reference or id; with it off, the assistant is told that editing and moving reach the workspace at its next stable release and to describe the change instead. The closing sentence reads "You never write to the project yourself: every change reaches it through a card the person clicks." The gate is `release.FeatureAssistantEdits` (`assistant-project-edits`, ShippedIn 0.5.0 — 0.4.0 and 0.4.1 were cut by other work while this was open) resolved by `memberFeatureEnabled(orgID, launchedBy, key)` — the launching member's channel and stable release, as `featureEnabled` does for a request.

**Frontend.** `suggestionDrafts.ts` reads the three kinds into `artifact` (with `place{parentRef, afterRef}`), `edit` and `move` plans, refusing an unknown type, an empty edit, an emptied title, a move that names nowhere or both before and after; references are upper-cased as they are minted. `utils/artifactOrder.ts` is the pure placement planner: `planPlacement(artifacts, sourceId, {parentId?, beforeId?, afterId?, position?})` produces the same `MovePlan` a drag does (no move into its own subtree, an anchor must be under the destination, a no-op is null) and `saveSiblingOrder` writes it the same way (the sibling group renumbered 1..n, only changed rows written, the moved artifact re-parented). `applySuggestion.ts` resolves a reference or an artifact id against a working copy of the project that every write folds its result into, so a later card in a batch can place something after, or move, what an earlier card created; an edit sends only the fields named and merges attributes over the current ones because the API replaces attributes wholesale; a placed artifact is created last under its parent (`nextSortOrder`) and then placed after its anchor. It also exports the shared gate (`ASSISTANT_EDITS_FEATURE`, `isProjectEditKind`, `GATED_REASON`). `GuidedChatPanel` labels the three kinds *Apply change*, *Move* and *+ Add to project* wherever they are shown, summarises an edit field by field and a move by destination, and takes `applyTarget: 'wizard' | 'project'` for the wizard-shaped kinds' labels. `ChatterPanel` passes `applyTarget="project"`, keeps the applied keys so a card cannot write twice, and answers a gated kind with the reason when `useFeature` is off. `GuidedWizard.handleApplySuggestions` routes the three kinds through `applySuggestionsToProject` against a fresh artifact list (refreshing the draft list afterwards, gated the same way) and the wizard kinds through the form, returning one result per card in order and recording both in the session's applied keys.

**Audit.** `e2e/tools/phone-audit.js` gained the `notes-assistant` screen, a transcript carrying the three cards (also rendered by the `guided-assistant` screen, where they now carry their buttons), and a features mock placed ahead of the org catch-all (which had been answering `{}` and crashing every `useFeature` since 0.3.0). The panel's 10–11px labels and 22px controls were raised to the 12px/24px floors.

artifacts.title: Platform admin page, admin listings and admin promotion
artifacts.body: `internal/api/admin_handlers.go` registers `GET /api/v1/admin/workspaces` (every live workspace from `orgs.Service.ListAll` with its member count), `GET /api/v1/admin/users` (every account, admins first, without hashes) and `PUT /api/v1/admin/users/{id}/admin` behind `requirePlatformAdmin` (401/403). `users.Service.SetAdmin` loads the account, refuses `ErrLastAdmin` when it would leave no admin, and writes through `UpdateUser`; the handler refuses self-demotion. `frontend/src/views/PlatformAdmin.tsx` at `/admin` (account menu → Platform admin, shown to `is_admin` accounts only) renders the two tables with a plan selector wired to `PUT /api/v1/orgs/{id}/plan` and Make admin / Remove buttons, each behind a confirm dialog. Manual chapter `platform-admin`.

artifacts.title: Default workspace: users.default_org_id, resolver fallback and the settings control
artifacts.body:
Built (REQ-156, gated under REQ-137 as `default-workspace`, ShippedIn 0.6.0).

**Storage.** Migration 0040 adds `users.default_org_id UUID` (nullable, `REFERENCES organizations(id) ON DELETE SET NULL`, added tolerantly so a re-run is harmless). `users.User.DefaultOrgID` (`default_org_id` on the wire, so `GET /auth/me` carries it); `Repository.SetDefaultOrg(userID, orgID)` writes `NULLIF($2,'')::uuid` and the user columns read it back with `COALESCE(default_org_id::text, '')`. The domain service is a pass-through: whether the member may land there is the caller's check, since the users layer does not know workspaces.

**Resolution.** `AuthMiddleware.resolveActiveOrg` keeps its order — the `X-OpenV-Org` header, then the session's own switch (`sessions.active_org_id`, set by `POST /orgs/{id}/activate`) — and, before falling back to the personal workspace, tries `user.DefaultOrgID` if the member is still a member of it (`orgService.IsMember`). A fresh sign-in has no session switch, so the choice decides where it lands; a switch made during the session wins for that session; a choice the member has since left falls through to the personal workspace rather than failing every request.

**Endpoint.** `internal/api/default_workspace_handlers.go`: `GET /api/v1/me/default-workspace` → `{org_id}`; `PUT` with `{org_id}`: `""` clears; a workspace the caller does not belong to, or that does not exist, is `404` with one message so the endpoint cannot enumerate workspaces; the personal workspace's id is stored as `""` (it is what the absence of a choice means, and a stored personal id could go stale); a company workspace is gated by its own channel through `featureEnabled(r, orgID, release.FeatureDefaultWorkspace)` and answers `403` with `featureGateMessage` when closed. Own-user only: the update is keyed on the session user.

**Client.** `utils/activeOrg.ts` `pickActiveOrg(orgs, tabOrg, serverActive, lastUsed)` is what `App.tsx` opens in: this tab's session-storage workspace (two tabs, two workspaces, each surviving a reload), then the server's `active_org` (the session's switch, else the member's default, else personal), then the browser's last-used workspace, then personal, then anything. The server's answer now outranks the browser's memory, so a chosen default is honoured on a new sign-in even in a browser that last sat in the personal workspace; before, local storage won and a member could never land anywhere but where that browser was last. `UserSettingsPanel` gains a *Default workspace* card after *Appearance*: a select of "My personal workspace" plus every company workspace the member belongs to (the store's `orgs`), saving through `defaultWorkspaceAPI.set` and reflecting the answer on `currentUser.default_org_id`; when `useFeature('default-workspace')` is off it shows "Reaches this workspace with its next stable release" instead of the control, and a server refusal is shown under the card.

**Docs.** `docs/api-spec.md` (the two rows, the gate key), `docs/data-model.md` (the column), the manual's *Getting started → Workspaces → Where you start*, and the layout audit's features mock (the gate on, so the `user-settings` screen renders the control).

artifacts.title: Figure titles: attachment title column, rename as a figure version, gallery rename
artifacts.body:
Migration 0041 `attachment_titles` adds `attachments.title` and `attachment_versions.title` (`VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL DEFAULT ''`). `attachments.Attachment.Title` and `Version.Title` carry it; `Attachment.Name()` is the display name (trimmed title, else the uploaded filename, else the stored filename), used by the report caption (`figureCaption`) and the figure feed notes. `Repository.Rename(id, title, by)` runs one transaction: `UPDATE attachments SET version = version + 1, title = $2 … RETURNING` the current file fields, then inserts an `attachment_versions` row copying those fields with the new title, `created_by` and `created_at`; `AddVersion` now reads the title back from the row so a new image carries it into its version row. `Service.RenameFigure` trims and bounds the title (`MaxTitleLen`, `ErrTitleTooLong`).

`PUT /api/v1/attachments/{id}` `{title}` (`RenameAttachment` in `internal/api/handlers.go`): editor on the artifact's project; `403` with the feature gate message when the workspace's channel has not received `figure-titles` (ShippedIn 0.6.0); an unchanged title answers the current attachment without writing; otherwise the figure is renamed, the artifact takes an attribute-free `UpdateArtifact` (as a new image gives it) and a `figure-change` note records the old and new names and the version numbers. The upload endpoint accepts an optional `title` form field.

Frontend: `attachmentAPI.rename`; `ImageGallery` shows `figureName()` under the reference, offers ✎ (a prompt dialog) when the gate is open and the gallery is editable with an `onRename` handler, and labels each history entry `uploaded`, `renamed` or `new image` (`versionKind`, by comparing file paths) with the title it carried. `ArtifactEditor` passes `onRenameAttachment` through; `ModuleView.handleRenameAttachment` calls the API and reloads the artifact.

artifacts.title: Password reset: token table, uninformative request, admin mint, reset page
artifacts.body:
Migration 0042 `password_resets` (id, user_id, token_hash unique, delivery `email`|`admin`, issued_by, expires_at, used, created_at). `users.PasswordReset`; `Repository.SavePasswordReset` (discards the account's unused links first, so one is live) and `ConsumePasswordReset` (`UPDATE … SET used WHERE token_hash AND NOT used AND expires_at > now RETURNING`, the single-use guard). `Service.IssuePasswordReset(userID, delivery, issuedBy)` refuses an unknown id (`ErrUserNotFound`) and an account with no password hash (`ErrNoPassword`), and picks the TTL by delivery (`PasswordResetTTL` 1 h, `AdminPasswordResetTTL` 24 h). `Service.ResetPassword(token, password)` checks `MinPasswordLength` before consuming, bcrypts and stores the hash, `DeleteSessionsForUser(id, "")`, and `MarkEmailVerified` only for `email` delivery.

`internal/api/password_reset_handlers.go`: `POST /auth/password-reset` validates the address, answers `409 reset_email_unavailable` when the mailer is off, throttles on `authIPLimiter` and the new per-address `passwordResetLimiter` (`OPENV_PASSWORD_RESET_BURST`/`_REFILL_PER_HOUR`, 3/6), then answers `202 {sent_to}` and runs lookup, mint and send in a goroutine (`sendPasswordResetFor`), logging failures. `POST /auth/password-reset/confirm` throttles per IP and maps `ErrWeakPassword` → `400 weak_password`, `ErrResetInvalid` → `400 reset_invalid`, success → `204` with no session. `POST /admin/users/{id}/password-reset` (`requirePlatformAdmin`) mints an admin link, answers `{link, expires_at}` once, logs admin and user ids, `404`/`409 no_password`. `GET /auth/config` gains `password_reset_email`. `notify.PasswordResetLink` (`/reset-password?token=`) and `RenderPasswordResetEmail`.

Frontend: `authAPI.requestPasswordReset/confirmPasswordReset`, `adminAPI.issuePasswordReset`, `apiErrorCode`. `Login` gains a `forgot` mode (Forgot your password? → address form → the same message for every address; the administrator note when `password_reset_email` is false) and a `?reset=done` notice. New `ResetPassword` view at `/reset-password?token=` (public path): password twice against the server's `min_password_length`, `reset_invalid` → a dead-link page with a link to request another; success → `/login?reset=done`. `PlatformAdmin`: a *Reset link* button per password account, confirmation, the link shown once with Copy. Feature key `password-reset` (0.6.0) registered for the features list; the flow runs before any workspace exists to gate on, so it is unconditional.

artifacts.title: Pool load band on the member payload
artifacts.body:
`PoolCounts.Load()` in `internal/domain/runnersessions` reduces the pool's node, idle and leased counts to a single band, and the member-facing runner-session payload carries that band under `pool_load` in place of the former `pool` object. `internal/api/runner_session_handlers.go` performs the reduction before serialization, so the counts never reach a member's response — including the 503 body returned when the pool is full, which shares the payload shape.

Thresholds: green above a 0.30 idle share, red below 0.05, amber between them, and a separate `unavailable` band when the pool reports no online node. Amber spans the whole middle rather than only 0.05-0.10 because the pool runs at single-digit node counts, where one free node out of five is a 0.20 share; without the fill the amber band would be unreachable below roughly ten nodes.

`unavailable` is kept distinct from `red` because the card's two messages differ: a deployment with no pool tells the member to use the connector path, while a full pool tells them to wait.

The frontend renders the band as a dot and a label (`RunnerPoolStatus` and `PoolLoadIndicator` in `frontend/src/components/org/CloudRunnerCard.tsx`). The label carries the meaning independently of the dot's colour, so the indicator survives a colour-blind reading and a screen reader.

The workspace-admin endpoint `GET /api/v1/orgs/{id}/runner-pool` is unchanged and still returns `PoolCounts`, which is what an operator needs in order to size the pool.

artifacts.title: To-dos as a view over work items, with the raising note recorded on the item
artifacts.body:
Satisfies REQ-160.

**A to-do is a work item, not a new entity.** `work_items` already carries a title, a description, an assignee (user, agent or team), a due date and a board column. Building a second table would have meant two lists of the same work, two places to mark something done, and a board that disagrees with the to-do page by lunchtime. The To-dos page is therefore a second arrangement of the board's rows, not a second store: it reads `GET /api/v1/projects/{id}/work-items` and groups client-side. The item's board column *is* its status.

**The note link lives on the work item.** Migration 43 adds `work_items.source_chatter_id UUID`, with a partial index on the rows that have one — only to-dos raised from notes carry it, and the notes panel is the only reader. The direction is chosen by cardinality: a note raises at most one to-do, a to-do comes from at most one note, and the item is the row that already changes when the work moves. It is written once at creation and never by `Update`, so editing a card cannot detach it from its origin.

**The note's status chip is composed at read time, never stored.** `GET /api/v1/chatter` fills two display-only fields on each entry: `mentions` (the project members its @names resolve to) and `todo` (`work_item_id`, `title`, `status`, `assignee_id`, `assignee_name`). One `ListBySourceChatterIDs` query covers the whole feed rather than one lookup per note, and one membership read serves both fields. A failure of either leaves the feed intact and logs — a missing chip is a worse page, a 500 is no page. Because the status is read each time, moving a card on the board changes what an old note says.

**Mention matching is shared, not re-implemented.** `internal/domain/mentions` now owns the rules the notifier had privately: the `@([\w.-]+)` token scan, and the handles a member answers to (full name without spaces, first name, email local part). Two things now act on the same text — the notifier telling someone they were mentioned, and the panel offering a to-do for whoever the note names — and a note that notifies Dave but offers a to-do for nobody would read as a bug. The notifier was refactored onto the package rather than duplicated.

**Raising is explicit.** The panel shows *Add to-do*, pre-filled from the mention and the note's first line; a bare @mention creates nothing. An automatic rule would have turned "thanks @dave" into a board card. The full note becomes the description so detail is not lost, and the artifact the note is on is linked to the item.

**Two checks guard the note link.** `CreateWorkItem` refuses a `source_chatter_id` whose note is not in the same project (400), resolving it through the new `chatter.Service.GetEntry`; and the feed composer independently skips any work item whose `project_id` differs from the project being read. Either alone would do; the cost of being wrong is one project's work item title rendered inside another's, which is not a check to leave single.

**Ordering is by attention, not by the board.** `ATTENTION_ORDER` in `components/kanban/columns.ts` reads in-progress, review, todo, backlog, done — the board's left-to-right order starts at Backlog, which is the wrong end for a list of what someone owes. That module is also now the single source of the five column labels and colours, shared by the board, the page and the note chip.

Gated on the `todo-list` feature key (0.8.0), which hides both the nav entry and the *Add to-do* control.

artifacts.title: Figure restore as a forward-only version, recorded with what it brought back
artifacts.body:
Satisfies REQ-50 (the restore clauses).

**Forward-only, matching how an artifact restore already behaves.** `AttachmentRepository.Restore(attachmentID, version, by)` reads the target version row and writes its image and title as a *new* version (`current + 1`). Nothing is deleted and the counter never rewinds. The alternative reading of "revert" — rewind to version N and drop what came after — would destroy the record of what a figure showed while a requirement was reviewed or a baseline captured against it, which is the one thing this product exists to keep. The manual already promised this shape for artifacts ("Restoring creates a new version with the old content; nothing is lost"), so figures now read the same way.

**The title travels with the image.** The `UPDATE` sets `title` as well as the file columns. Restoring the drawing while leaving a later rename in place would show one figure under another figure's name — the one failure mode that would make a restore actively misleading rather than merely incomplete.

**The stored file is shared, not copied.** The new version row points at the target's `file_path`. Every version's file is already kept for the life of the figure and nothing deletes them individually, so a copy would only add bytes and a way to drift. The consequence is that a restore is indistinguishable from a re-upload by path — which is why migration 44 adds `attachment_versions.restored_from INT`, written with the version that was brought back.

`restored_from` is not bookkeeping: `versionKind` in the gallery derives a history entry's description by comparing file paths with the previous entry, and without the column a restore reads as "new image", or as "renamed" when the restored picture happens to match what is showing. Both describe the wrong event. The frontend checks `restored_from` first.

**One transaction, with the figure locked.** `SELECT … FOR UPDATE` on the attachment precedes the checks, so a concurrent upload cannot advance the version between the "is this already current?" test and the write. A figure whose attachment row advanced without a matching version row would be a figure with no record of what it currently shows.

**Refusals are distinct and neither writes.** `ErrNoSuchVersion` (404) covers both a version the figure never had and a figure that does not exist; `ErrAlreadyCurrent` (409) covers asking for the state it is already in — not a mistake worth an error page, but not worth a version that changed nothing either.

**API and UI.** `POST /api/v1/attachments/{id}/versions/{version}/restore`, editor role, matching version upload: it changes what the figure shows. The gallery's history dialog gains *Restore* on every row but the current one, behind a confirm that says what will happen, and the figure's own thumbnail and the artifact's figures are reloaded afterwards through a new `onRestored` callback — otherwise the gallery keeps showing the superseded image behind the open dialog.

Gated on the `figure-revert` feature key (0.8.0).

artifacts.title: Side panel modes: the cycle that does not close under you, and a strip you can find
artifacts.body:
`frontend/src/components/panelMode.ts` is the whole model, shared by the project navigation (ProjectLayout) and the artifact notes panel (ModuleView), so the two cannot drift. A mode is pinned, autohide or hidden; `nextPanelMode` cycles them; `panelIsOpen(mode, hovered, revealed)` decides whether the panel occupies the screen; `panelTakesSpace` decides whether it takes width from the document or floats over it; `loadPanelMode`/`savePanelMode` remember the choice per person and per panel in localStorage, defaulting to pinned so nothing moves for somebody who never chose.

`revealed` is the reader asking for a panel back by clicking its edge strip. Hover deliberately does not open a hidden panel — that is the difference between hidden and auto-hide — so without an explicit reveal the strip would be a button that does nothing.

Two defects in that mechanism, both reported:

Cycling closed the panel under the reader (issue #362). Both cycle handlers called setRevealed(false) and setHovered(false), so choosing Auto-hide or Hidden shut the panel on the spot and took the mode button — which lives inside the panel — off the screen with it. Reaching the third option meant finding the edge strip first, and anybody who wanted to compare the modes had to leave the panel between each one. `revealAfterModeChange(next)` now answers true for any mode that would close the panel, and the handlers pass it to setRevealed, so the panel stays put and the button keeps its place under the pointer. Pinned asks for no reveal: it is open by definition, and carrying a stale reveal into it would leave the next cycle unable to close anything. Dismissal is unchanged — click away, Escape, or the strip. A test walks the full cycle asserting the panel is open at every step.

The strip was not findable (issue #363). It was 10 px wide with a 12 px chevron and no border, which reads as chrome rather than as the only way back from Hidden. `panelStripWidth(coarsePointer)` gives 24 px on a mouse and 32 px on a finger; the chevron sits in a `.panel-edge-strip-knob` — bordered, rounded, 20×28 — so it looks like a control before anybody hovers it; and the strip is a real `<button>` with `panelStripLabel` as its accessible name ("Show the notes panel"), `aria-expanded`, and a focus ring. The floating panel's offset reads the same helper, so the panel still sits flush against the strip at either width.

artifacts.title: Entitlement resolution folded into three-layer limit resolution
artifacts.body:
Org.Plan became Org.BilledPlan (the JSON field is still "plan"): the plan a workspace is billed for, which is no longer the plan it is entitled to once a subscription can lapse. The rename made the compiler audit every read site once — the hosted-runner provisioner's fallback now reads the entitled plan; the release-channel and open-source checks correctly keep reading the billed one.

EntitledPlan() is the one place billing status touches enforcement. It returns the billed plan while Billing.Status is none, trialing, active or past due, and PlanSingle otherwise — an unrecognised status included, mirroring PlanDefaults' stance that an unknown plan is never unlimited. EffectiveLimits() reads it where it read the plan column, so every existing enforcement helper (seats, projects, shared workspaces, uploads, evidence, runner leases, hosted-runner resources) follows without knowing billing exists. The self-hosted override still runs after it, and the workspace and deployment layers still win, so a grandfathering override survives a lapse.

Past due keeps the paid plan with no local grace clock. The provider's dunning schedule is the grace period; its terminal action — which must be cancellation, not "mark unpaid" — is what ends the entitlement. A second clock here would only disagree with it.

Flags join the limits catalogue as a Kind of their own: hosted_automation, teams and workspace_budget are bools resolved through the same three layers, so a workspace override grandfathers them exactly as it does a count. A flag has to be a distinct kind because 0 already means unlimited. ParseLimits accepts a bool for a flag key and nothing else; Allowed() reads an absent flag as allowed, the house rule that a limit check is never the reason a legitimate action fails. They ship on for every plan.

Migration 45 adds the mirrored snapshot to organizations (customer, subscription and item refs, currency, status, interval, seats, cancel-at-period-end, grandfathered, period end, synced-at) with unique partial indexes on the customer and subscription refs. ApplyBillingState is one conditional UPDATE carrying three rules: an older read never overwrites a newer one (WHERE plan_synced_at <= readAt; zero rows is a success), a granted plan is never moved by a subscription, and the first move from a nightly-only plan onto a channel-choosing one writes a nightly release-channel override — without it the plan flip would put the new subscriber on the stable channel with no stable release turned on, closing every gated feature at once.

Two existing bugs closed on the way: OrgRepository.UpdateOrg wrote plan and limits from the in-memory struct, a read-modify-write that could put a stale plan back over a concurrent billing write, and now writes the name only; and SetPlan refuses to grant enterprise or open_source over a live subscription.

artifacts.title: Price registry, Stripe client, reconcile loop and public catalogue
artifacts.body:
internal/billing is the sync path; internal/billing/stripe the provider. Neither is reachable unless STRIPE_SECRET_KEY is set, and a key on a self-hosted deployment is ignored with a warning rather than refused, so a copied env template cannot lock somebody out of their own install. With no provider the service is nil-safe and inert, every billing route answers 404 billing_unavailable, and TestSelfHostedNeverContactsStripe-style tests assert nothing dials out.

The price registry (OPENV_STRIPE_PRICES, a JSON array of {price, plan, interval}) is the only thing that turns a subscription into a plan. It accepts business_lite and business, month and year, one price per pair, and refuses everything else at parse time — enterprise, open_source, self_host and the legacy aliases are granted, never bought. A product's name, nickname or metadata is never read to decide a plan. Prices are confirmed against the provider (existence under this key, interval, per-licence billing, amounts per currency via currency_options) on the first reconcile and every tick, never at boot, so boot never waits on the provider; until a confirmation succeeds the catalogue is unsellable.

The Stripe client is hand-rolled: nine calls through one do() that carries the auth and version headers, retries only rate limits, server errors and transport failures, never repeats a write without an idempotency key, parses only the fields the platform reads, unwraps a 404 to ErrNotFound and never logs a body. SetCancelAtPeriodEnd carries a fresh idempotency key per attempt because Stripe replays a reused key's original answer for a day, which would make on → off → on stick at off.

The reconcile loop runs at boot and every OPENV_BILLING_RECONCILE_MINUTES (5): it lists every subscription, applies each with the time it was read, re-reads any stored subscription the listing missed, marks subscriptions with an open dispute as lapsed (the charge expanded through to its invoice is the only route from a dispute to a subscription), cancels a live subscription whose workspace no longer exists, reports the oldest snapshot's age as billing_sync_stale_seconds, and re-confirms prices. A workspace is found by its stored subscription ref, then by the openv_org_id the subscription carries; never by email or name. A subscription naming a workspace that already holds a different live subscription is not bound. A price the registry does not know, or a subscription with more than one item, changes nothing and increments billing_unknown_price_total. Every failed step leaves the last known state in place.

Three routes, registered on every deployment so the route inventory does not depend on the environment: GET /api/v1/public/plans serves the last confirmed catalogue from memory, cached for five minutes, and never calls the provider; GET /api/v1/orgs/{id}/billing gives an admin the billed plan, entitled plan and snapshot without a provider id; POST /api/v1/orgs/{id}/billing/refresh re-reads one subscription now, bounded per workspace, and answers 503 billing_upstream with Retry-After when the provider fails, the workspace unchanged. Deleting a workspace schedules its subscription to end with the paid period; restoring it resumes the subscription; a purged workspace's subscription is cancelled by the loop as an orphan.

The pricing page reads the public catalogue once and, for a tier with a planKey the platform prices, shows the monthly amount — GBP where offered, per member where the plan is per seat, "excluding VAT" where the price is — in place of "Coming soon". No price lives in the repository.

artifacts.title: Hosted checkout, session binding, in-place plan change and the portal
artifacts.body:
`internal/billing/checkout.go`: `Checkout` creates the provider customer once per workspace (idempotency key `openv:cust:<org>:v1`, currency locked at first purchase), then a checkout session keyed `openv:co:<org>:<plan>:<interval>:<currency>:<5-minute bucket>` with `client_reference_id` = the workspace id, the trial attached only while `users.billing_trial_used_at` is null, promotion codes on, tax on. `BindCheckoutSession` re-reads the session, refuses one naming another workspace (`403 checkout_mismatch`), applies the subscription through `ApplyBillingState` (which pins the nightly channel override on the first move onto a choosable plan), marks the buyer's trial used, and cancels a competing live subscription. `ChangePlan` updates the one subscription item's price and quantity (Lite 1, Business the seat count) with a fresh idempotency key. `PortalURL` opens the configured portal configuration, return URL the Billing tab.

Routes (`internal/api/billing_handlers.go`): `POST /orgs/{id}/billing/checkout` (feature `workspace-billing`), `/change`, `/portal`; `refresh` takes `session_id`. Admin only, rate limited (`OPENV_BILLING_WRITE_BURST`/`_REFILL_PER_HOUR`), 404 without a provider.

`frontend/src/components/org/OrgBillingTab.tsx`: per-status rendering, the plan picker with a computed preview, checkout by redirect, return handling that binds the session and strips the parameters, portal and change-plan buttons.

artifacts.title: Coalescing seat queue with reconcile drift repair
artifacts.body:
`internal/billing/seats.go`: `SeatsChanged(orgID)` is a non-blocking send on a 1024-slot channel; one goroutine drains it into a set every two seconds and pushes each workspace once (`FlushSeats`). A push applies only to a live Business subscription with an item ref: quantity = members + pending invitations (the handler's `countOrgSeats`), floor 1, refused and counted above `OPENV_BILLING_MAX_SEATS` (default 500). After a push the subscription is re-read and applied so the snapshot shows the new quantity. `Reconcile` calls `repairSeatDrift` over every billed workspace and reports `billing_seat_drift`.

Call sites (`internal/api`): `addOrInviteToOrg` after the add or the invitation, `RemoveOrgMember`, `RevokeOrgInvitation`; not on acceptance (the invitation was already a seat), never inline. Metrics `billing_seat_drift` and `billing_seat_push_refused_total`.

artifacts.title: Tier values behind the grandfather date, alpha-terms overrides, flag gates and the read-only chokepoint
artifacts.body:
`internal/domain/orgs/limits.go`: `PlanDefaults` lays the tier values over each plan's alpha defaults only while `SetTiersEnforced(true)`; `AlphaTerms()` is the per-workspace override (counts 0, flags true, minutes 0); `OverPlan(limits, usage)` names the count limits past their ceiling; `CheckFlag` refuses a flag the plan lacks with a `LimitError{Flag: true}`. New key `hosted_runner_minutes_month`.

`cmd/server/main.go`: `OPENV_BILLING_GRANDFATHER_BEFORE` (RFC 3339) runs `OrgRepository.GrandfatherBefore` (`limits = $terms || limits`, `plan_grandfathered = TRUE`, `WHERE created_at < $1 AND NOT plan_grandfathered`, no deleted_at predicate; fatal on failure) and then throws the switch.

`internal/api/limits.go` and `authz.go`: `requireOrgRole` and `requireProjectRole` call `requireWritable` for POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE, which answers `403 plan_read_only` when `overPlan` is non-empty unless the route was registered through `alwaysWritable` (delete workspace, remove member, revoke invitation, delete project, import, the billing routes). Gates: `checkFlag` at `CreateHostedRunner`, the hosted branch of `ClaimAgentRun`, `CreateOrgTeam`, `GrantProjectTeamAccess`, `GetOrgUsage` and the budget write; `leaseMinutesAllowed` at `StartRunnerSession`/`ExtendRunnerSession` with `RunnerSessionRepository.MinutesUsed`. `notify.MinutesMonitor` alerts admins at 80%/100% through `ClaimMinutesAlert` (migration 47). The limits response carries `read_only`, `over_plan`, the flags with `included`, and the month's minutes; the Limits and Billing tabs show the read-only banner.

artifacts.title: Authorization matrix suite
artifacts.body: Automated Go suite exercising the role ladder: platform admin, org admin, direct grants, team grants, run-own-project, worker org scoping. Pass = every matrix cell returns the expected allow/deny.

artifacts.title: Tenant isolation end-to-end
artifacts.body: Live check with two accounts in different orgs: all cross-org reads and writes return 403/404; org directories and worker keys stay scoped; team-grant escalation raises effective role as designed.

artifacts.title: Personal key rotation suite
artifacts.body: Automated suite: minting a new personal key revokes the previous one; revoked keys fail resolution; each member holds at most one active personal key per workspace.

artifacts.title: Hosted token-mode smoke test
artifacts.body: openv-worker image boots with an API key env, reports the CLI logged in via API-key mode without any interactive login, and excludes repo-access runs from its claims.

artifacts.title: Copilot prompt isolation test
artifacts.body: The assistant prompt declares the product profile, wizard state, transcript and the artifact on screen as content and never as instructions, fences the state block and the artifact block, and places the trust rules ahead of every scrap of that content.

artifacts.title: Lease teardown and credential scope suite
artifacts.body: Ending a lease revokes its credential and sends the node to draining before it is released; a stale release from a finished lease cannot free a node that has since been leased again; a session key never displaces the member's own connector key while still counting as their runner for routing. The pool key authenticates a pool node and carries no workspace, user or worker identity, and a wrong key is rejected; the pool endpoints refuse a member session and a workspace worker key. End to end against a live API and pool node: after the lease ends the node's per-lease home is removed, the key is revoked, and a second lease on the same node reports the vendor CLI as installed but signed out.

artifacts.title: Production hardening probe
artifacts.body: Manual, against the deployed API and frontend with an unauthenticated HTTP client. 1. Send eight failed password sign-ins within two seconds from one address; expect a rate-limited response before the eighth. 2. Request the frontend root, a static asset and an API response; expect nosniff, a frame-denying header, a referrer policy and strict transport security on each, and a content security policy without unsafe-inline or unsafe-eval on the frontend. 3. Send a preflight and a plain request with a foreign Origin; expect no Access-Control-Allow-Origin header. 4. Request /metrics without credentials; expect 401 when a metrics token is configured. 5. Post an empty registration; expect a validation error, and confirm whether registration is open for the deployment.

artifacts.title: Hardening middleware and credential throttle suite
artifacts.body: Go suites in internal/api and internal/domain/providers: every response carries nosniff, a frame-denying header, a referrer policy and a CSP, with HSTS only when the deployment declares TLS; a wildcard, empty or null CORS origin is refused at construction and only the configured origin receives credentialed allow headers, a foreign preflight receiving none; an oversized JSON body is cut off with a MaxBytesError while a multipart body passes the middleware untouched, so an upload handler's own larger ceiling is the one in force (issue #364); an upload over the cap is answered 413 and leaves no partial file on disk, one at the cap is stored whole and reports its real size, and the head handed to the format check is a full 512 bytes of the start of the file; the per-file upload ceiling follows the workspace's plan where no operator override is set and the OPENV_MAX_UPLOAD_MB override wins where it is, a malformed override falling back to the plan rather than to "no cap"; every capped plan allows at least 100 MB and the uncapped plans ration nothing; PNG bytes pass as PNG, HTML bytes fail as PNG or SVG, an SVG root or XML prolog passes as SVG, TIFF passes by magic number only; an SVG is served as an attachment inside a sandbox CSP and a raster image inline with img-src self; three wrong passwords close an account so both a wrong and a right password are then refused with 429 and Retry-After while another account from the same address still signs in; correct sign-ins never charge the account; an address is throttled across accounts; a second registration from one address is refused; nil throttles allow everything; the invite-token segment of public interview paths is redacted and other paths are left alone; a provider setting naming a variable outside the key catalog is refused and never persisted while every catalogued name and blank are accepted, and every provider's default variable is in the catalog.

artifacts.title: Requirements gap analysis 2026-09-06
artifacts.body:
Scope: the live **OpenV Platform** project (64 requirements, 11 needs,
16 design items, 33 test cases, baseline *2026-09-04 One download, chosen
and filtered*) challenged in its entirety against the feature set actually
shipped on `master` at `cfabf06` (Railway `release` at the same head).

Method: a route-by-route, package-by-package inventory of the codebase
(≈265 HTTP routes, 36 domain packages, 23 schema migrations, 21 SPA views,
5 Playwright journeys, 29 MCP tools) was compared with every requirement
body, every need, and every test case's evidence claim. Findings are graded:

| Grade | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **G1 — shipped, unspecified** | A capability exists with no requirement stating it. It cannot be traced, baselined or verified. |
| **G2 — specified, stale** | The requirement text no longer matches the platform. |
| **G3 — specified, unverified** | A requirement whose test case does not exist, does not do what it claims, or whose verification is missing. |
| **G4 — specified, not built** | A requirement stated as binding for something that is not implemented. |
| **G5 — need under-served** | A stakeholder need whose derived requirements do not cover how the platform actually serves it. |

Every finding below has been recorded in the live project (new draft
artifacts, edits, comments and links) so the project itself carries the
result; this file is the off-instance record. See "How the result was
recorded" at the end.

## 1. Summary

| Grade | Count | Disposition |
|---|---|---|
| G1 shipped, unspecified | 19 capability groups | 25 new draft requirements (REQ-65 … REQ-89) + 14 new test cases (TC-34 … TC-47) added to the project |
| G2 stale | 6 | 4 requirement/design bodies updated; 2 tensions left as comments for the maintainer |
| G3 unverified | 18 requirements without a verifying test case; 1 test case overclaiming | Recorded as comments; 3 new test cases cover 4 of them |
| G4 not built | 2 (REQ-44 remote MCP; macOS connector in REQ-32) | Commented; REQ-44 left draft as a roadmap requirement |
| G5 need under-served | 3 needs (NEED-5, NEED-9, NEED-7 audit) | New requirements derive from them |

The requirement set is **strong where the last four weeks of work landed**
(figures, downloads, quality rules, runner leasing, agent seeds) and **thin
where the platform grew earlier and quietly**: the review workflow, baseline
comparison, impact analysis, search, notifications, budgets, run resilience,
import/templates, observability and backups are all shipped and untraced.
Security is specified by five requirements and verified by six test cases; the
companion security assessment records what those leave uncovered.

## 2. G1 — shipped but unspecified

Each row is a capability found in the code with no requirement stating it.
The "recorded as" column is the artifact created in the live project.

| # | Capability (evidence) | Under | Recorded as |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Artifact status workflow** — draft → in_review → approved → superseded, validated transitions, `PUT /artifacts/{id}/status`; approval clears link suspicion (`internal/domain/artifacts/status.go`) | HDG-3 | REQ-65 |
| 2 | **Suspect links and the review queue** — editing either end of a link flags it suspect until a reviewer confirms it (`PUT /links/{id}/confirm`); `/projects/{id}/review-queue` lists suspect links and in-review artifacts (migration 5, `ReviewQueue.tsx`, `e2e/tests/review-queue.spec.ts`) | HDG-3 | REQ-66; TC-34 |

| 5 | **Search** — trigram search across a workspace (`/api/v1/search`, migration 9), opt-in semantic search and duplicate-candidate detection over pgvector embeddings, env-gated and off by default (`internal/domain/embeddings`, migration 16, `/projects/{id}/duplicates`, `/reindex-embeddings`) | HDG-3 | REQ-68, REQ-69; TC-36, TC-37 |

"Draft test cases" launches the seeded test-case-author agent in proposal mode (`docs/agents.md`, `/test-runs/{id}/agent-run`, `/projects/{id}/draft-test-cases`) | HDG-5 | REQ-74, REQ-75; TC-45 |

Also shipped and unspecified, recorded as one requirement each or folded into
the rows above: generic OIDC sign-in (folded into REQ-18), interview persona
linking and invite expiry/revocation (folded into REQ-8), the in-app manual
and contextual help, the global search box, theme switching, workspace member

## 3. G2 — stale requirements

| Ref | What is stale | Action taken |
|---|---|---|
