The absolute wording contradicts two other requirements. | Comment left; recommended rewording: proposal mode is the default, direct mode is an explicit per-agent choice by a workspace admin. |
| REQ-20 Lean agent context | "shall not feed agents large prompt contexts or requirement documents" — REQ-41 and REQ-49 deliberately place the product profile, wizard state, transcript and the artifact on screen in the assistant prompt, and the V&V Assistant carries WebSearch/WebFetch. Not a contradiction in practice (the content is bounded and fenced) but the text reads as one. | Comment left; recommended rewording bounds what a prompt may carry rather than forbidding content outright. |
| REQ-53 / REQ-64 | Both specify the side-panel states; REQ-64 restates part of REQ-53 with a differing rule (a hidden panel opens on click, not hover). | Comment left; REQ-64 should `decomposes-to` from REQ-53 or the two should merge. |
| `docs/operations.md` | Says hosted-runner containers run with **no resource caps**; `docs/agents.md`, `docker-compose.prod.yml` and `internal/hosting/provisioner.go` apply memory/CPU caps from plan limits. | Doc fixed in this change. |

## 4. G3 — specified but unverified

Before this work `get_vv_gaps` reported **no gaps at all** while
`get_vv_coverage` listed nine requirements as *uncovered* (REQ-18, REQ-25,
REQ-35, REQ-36, REQ-44, REQ-51, REQ-53, REQ-54, REQ-58). The gap tool flags a
missing test case only for requirements whose method is `test`; a
`demonstration` or `analysis` requirement with no evidence and no
verification status is silent there while the coverage rollup calls it
uncovered. That disagreement between two V&V views of the same project is
itself a platform finding (REQ-12 says gaps are "actionable"; a requirement
the rollup calls uncovered should appear in them). Beyond it, two things were
hidden:

**Requirements with no verifying test case at all** (18): REQ-2, REQ-4,
REQ-5, REQ-13, REQ-14, REQ-18, REQ-19, REQ-20, REQ-22, REQ-23, REQ-24,
REQ-25, REQ-26, REQ-35, REQ-44, REQ-51, REQ-53, REQ-54. Most are
`demonstration`, which is legitimate for UI behaviour, but REQ-18, REQ-25
and REQ-44 carry no `verification_status` either, and REQ-26 (must,
verified) has only a design item behind it. New test cases now cover
REQ-5 and REQ-14 (TC-36 smoke journey), REQ-18 (TC-43) and REQ-22 (TC-42).

**A test case that overclaims**: TC-8 *Link rule validation suite* says
"Automated suite: each link type accepts its allowed from/to artifact types
and rejects all others". `internal/domain/links` has **no test files**; the
only coverage is indirect, in `internal/api/proposal_appliers_test.go`.
REQ-3 (must, method test) therefore has no direct evidence. Comment left on
TC-8.

**Evidence this session could produce**: the full Go suite passes
(`go test ./cmd/... ./internal/...`, 41 packages), which is the standing
evidence behind TC-1, TC-12, TC-14, TC-16, TC-17, TC-18, TC-20, TC-23,
TC-27, TC-28, TC-29 (unit half), TC-30 (automated half), TC-31 and TC-32.
Recorded as test run *2026-09-06 Assessment evidence* (29 results: 28 pass,
1 fail — the production hardening probe, see the security assessment). Not exercised here:
the Postgres-backed suites (skip without `OPENV_TEST_DATABASE_URL`), the
Playwright journeys and the client Jest suites (no built frontend in the
session), and every live check (TC-2, TC-5, TC-6, TC-7, TC-10, TC-11).

## 5. G4 — specified but not built

- **REQ-44 Remote MCP workspace connector** is written as "shall" but its own
  body ends "Not yet implemented"; DES-12 is "Proposed, not built". It should
  either carry a status the convention recognises (draft is right; it must
  not be approved or given a verification status) or move to a roadmap
  section. No test case exists; none should until it lands.
- **REQ-32 On-demand Agent Connector** promises "a single self-contained
  executable per OS"; `Dockerfile.api` builds Windows and Linux only, and
  `docs/railway.md` says macOS has no prebuilt download. Either the
  requirement names the two supported OSes or macOS is a known gap.

## 6. G5 — needs under-served by their requirements

- **NEED-9 Predictable agent execution** derives only REQ-27 and REQ-28
  (routing). The platform's actual answer to "starts reliably" is the retry
  chain, failure taxonomy and stale-run reaper (G1 #10) — now derived from
  NEED-9.
- **NEED-5 One view of human and AI work** derives only REQ-23. The
  notifications surface and board-driven runs (G1 #8, #14) are the other
  half of that view — now derived from NEED-5.
- **NEED-7 Audit-ready traceability** has no requirement for baseline
  comparison, impact analysis or the review queue (G1 #2, #3, #4) — the
  three features an auditor would actually use — now derived from NEED-7.

## 7. Conventions and hygiene observations

- The project's rule set is ISO 29148 "shall". 30 of the 64 requirements
  are `approved`; 34 are `draft`, including `must` requirements that have
  been verified for weeks (REQ-1, REQ-7, REQ-26, REQ-34, REQ-40, REQ-41…). A
  status pass would let the coverage rollup mean something.
- `priority` is unset on REQ-34 and REQ-35.
- The MoSCoW `priority` attribute and the body keyword are kept separate
  throughout, as the rule set requires.
- Test cases TC-31…TC-33 sit at the project root rather than under HDG-10 /
  HDG-14; moved under HDG-14 as part of this work.

## 8. How the result was recorded in the live project

1. New heading **HDG-16 Assessments** with two description artifacts holding
   this report and the security assessment.
2. New need **NEED-12 Run it myself without an operations team** (the
   operational and security requirements had no need to derive from).
3. New draft requirements REQ-65 … REQ-89 (G1) under the headings named in
   §2 and a new **HDG-17 Operations** heading, each with `derives-from` to
   the need it serves and `verifies` from a new test case (TC-34 … TC-47)
   where a suite exists. REQ-86 also `decomposes-to` from REQ-25.
4. Security: REQ-90 … REQ-100, HAZ-1 … HAZ-16 under **HDG-18 Security
   hazards**, and TC-48 — see the security assessment.
5. Body updates to REQ-2, REQ-3, REQ-18 and DES-1 (G2); comments on REQ-20,
   REQ-21, REQ-32, REQ-44, REQ-53 and TC-8. TC-31 … TC-33 moved under
   HDG-14.
6. Test run **2026-09-06 Assessment evidence** with the Go-suite results and
   the production probe.
7. Baseline **2026-09-06 Requirements and security assessment**.
8. A fresh export under `docs/exports/`.

artifacts.title: Security assessment 2026-09-06
artifacts.body:
Authorised defensive review of OpenV at `master` `cfabf06` (the same head
Railway `release` is serving), covering both deployment options:

- **Self-hosted** — `docker-compose.yml` + `docker-compose.prod.yml`,
  `Dockerfile.api`, `Dockerfile.worker`, `frontend/Dockerfile.prod` +
  `frontend/nginx.conf`, the backup sidecar.
- **Railway production** — the `OpenV` (API), `OpenV Frontend`, `OpenV
  Runner Pool` and `Postgres` services in the `incredible-solace` project.

Method: the security model claimed in `docs/architecture.md` and
`docs/operations.md` was verified claim by claim in code; every HTTP route
was traced for authentication and authorisation; `govulncheck` and `npm
audit --omit=dev` were run; the full Go suite was run; and the live
production API and frontend were probed with an unauthenticated client
(headers, CORS, throttling, metrics, registration, body limits). The Railway
service configuration was read through the Railway API (variable names only,
never values). No file was modified and no production data was written
outside the OpenV Platform project.

## 1. Verdict

**No authentication bypass and no cross-tenant access was found in the HTTP
API.** The multi-tenant model is coherent and consistently applied: bcrypt
passwords, every token from `crypto/rand` and stored as SHA-256, one
authorisation ladder on essentially every handler, object-to-project
resolution before any check (no IDOR found), org-scoped worker keys, a
least-privilege pool key, OIDC with nonce and state binding, sanitised 5xx
responses, parameterised SQL throughout, no raw HTML in the SPA.

The findings cluster in three places:

1. **The agent execution surface.** Vendor CLIs run with auto-approved edits
   (Gemini) or workspace-write sandboxes without a tool allowlist (Codex),
   while their prompts carry text from interview participants, repositories
   and web pages. Proposal gating protects OpenV data; it does not protect
   the runner host. This is the one **High**.
2. **Production configuration and hardening that the code supports but the
   deployment does not apply**: no throttling on sign-in, no security
   headers reaching the browser (an nginx `add_header` inheritance rule
   silently discards them), an open `/metrics`, open self-registration.
3. **Hygiene**: default secrets on the base compose file, a root API image,
   unencrypted on-host backups, a known-vulnerable Docker client module,
   invite tokens in the access log.

Every finding is recorded in the OpenV Platform project as a hazard
(HAZ-1 … HAZ-16 under *Security hazards*), each pointing at the draft
requirement (REQ-90 … REQ-100) that would close it, so `get_vv_gaps` shows
them as unmitigated until a design item mitigates them. The production
probe is test case TC-48 with a recorded **fail** in the run *2026-09-06
Assessment evidence*.

## 2. Findings

| ID | Severity | Affects | Finding | Closes with |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| SEC-1 | **High** | both | Prompt injection into auto-approving vendor CLIs. Gemini runs with `--approval-mode auto_edit` (`internal/runner/geminicli.go:112`), Codex with `--sandbox workspace-write` and no allowlist (`codexcli.go:140`), Claude Code with an allowlist only if the agent defines one (`claudecode.go:158`). The public interview transcript is concatenated into the interviewer prompt (`internal/api/suite_handlers.go:1528`) and that agent holds the OpenV tools; repo-access agents run in a real checkout; the V&V Assistant fetches the web. | REQ-91 |
| SEC-2 | Medium | self-hosted | Hosted-runner containers get memory/CPU caps only (`internal/hosting/docker.go:84-115`): no cap drop, no `no-new-privileges`, no pids limit, no dedicated network; provider keys in container env; the API holds the host Docker socket when enabled. | REQ-96 |
| SEC-3 | Medium | both | `provider_settings.api_key_env` is tenant-chosen and unvalidated (`internal/domain/providers/providers.go:66`); the worker does `os.Getenv` on it (`internal/runner/worker.go:368`), so a workspace admin can have `WORKER_API_KEY`, `RUNNER_POOL_KEY` or `DATABASE_URL` injected into an agent's environment. | REQ-92 |
| SEC-4 | Medium | self-hosted | Base compose runs Postgres as `postgres`/`postgres` with port 5432 published and `WORKER_API_KEY=dev-worker-key`; only the prod overlay makes them required. | REQ-97 |
| SEC-5 | Medium | both | No throttling on sign-in, registration, SSO callbacks or run launch (limiter exists only for public interview routes, `internal/api/handlers.go:233`). **Confirmed live**: 8 failed sign-ins in under 2 s, all 401, no back-off. | REQ-90 |
| SEC-6 | Medium | both | `image/svg+xml` accepted, uploader MIME stored, downloads served `inline` (`handlers.go:2275,2335`) → stored XSS on the API origin for a viewer opening the URL directly. Uploads use `io.ReadAll` with no `MaxBytesReader`; a 2 MB JSON body to sign-in was accepted on production. | REQ-93 |
| SEC-7 | Medium / Low on Railway | self-hosted | `govulncheck`: GO-2026-4887 and GO-2026-4883 in `github.com/docker/docker v28.5.2`, reachable via `internal/hosting`; six more advisories in required-not-called modules. Dormant on Railway (`HOSTED_RUNNERS=off`). | REQ-98 |
| SEC-8 | Low | both | `npm audit --omit=dev`: one high advisory in `fast-uri` (transitive, build-time). | REQ-98 |
| SEC-9 | Low | both | Public interview invite tokens are logged as part of the URL path (`internal/api/requestlog.go:62`). | REQ-97 |
| SEC-10 | Low | both | `Dockerfile.api` has no `USER`; the API runs as root in its container. | REQ-97 |
| SEC-11 | **Medium on Railway** / Low | both | **No browser security headers reach production.** `frontend/nginx.conf` sets X-Frame-Options, nosniff, Referrer-Policy and a CSP at server level, but every `location` block has its own `add_header`, and nginx discards inherited `add_header` directives in any location that sets one. Confirmed live: the frontend root, its static assets and every API response carry none of them, and there is no HSTS. The declared CSP is also permissive (`unsafe-inline`, `unsafe-eval`, any origin). | REQ-94 |
| SEC-12 | Low | self-hosted | Backups are plain `tar.gz` on the host with a full `pg_dump`; no encryption, no off-host copy. | REQ-88 |
| SEC-13 | Low | both (misconfig) | `CORS_ORIGIN="*"` reflects any origin *with* credentials (`cmd/server/main.go:636`). Production is configured with the exact origin; **confirmed live** that a foreign origin gets no CORS headers. | REQ-100 |
| SEC-14 | Low | Railway (config) | `/metrics` is open on production: 61 KB of Prometheus output to an unauthenticated client (Go runtime, per-route counts and latency, run gauges). `OPENV_METRICS_TOKEN` is not set on the service. | set the token |
| SEC-15 | Medium on Railway / Low | both | Self-registration is open on production with no verification, invitation or throttling; there is no way to close it. | REQ-95 |
| SEC-16 | Low | both | Sessions last 30 days with no idle expiry and no invalidation on password change (`internal/domain/users/users.go:25`). | REQ-99 |

## 3. Deployment-specific picture

### Railway production

| Aspect | State |
|---|---|
| Services | API, frontend, runner pool (1 replica each), Postgres; all online, no critical issues in the last 7 days; one failed pool deploy on 2026-09-05 since superseded. |
| Exposure | API and frontend have public domains; Postgres and the runner pool have none (private network only). |
| Variables (names only) | API: `CORS_ORIGIN`, `CROSS_SITE_COOKIES`, `DATABASE_URL`, `FRONTEND_URL`, `HOSTED_RUNNERS`, `OPENV_DATA_DIR`, `PUBLIC_URL`, `RUNNER_POOL_KEY`, `SECURE_COOKIES`, `UPLOADS_DIR`, `WORKER_API_KEY`. Not set: `OPENV_METRICS_TOKEN`, `OPENV_TRUST_PROXY`, any `OPENV_OIDC_*`/`GOOGLE_*`, `OPENV_SMTP_*`, `OPENV_EMBEDDING_*`. |
| Cookies | `SECURE_COOKIES` and `CROSS_SITE_COOKIES` set — session cookie is `SameSite=None; Secure`, which the split-domain layout requires. |
| TLS | Terminated at Railway's edge (HTTP/2). No HSTS from the origin. |
| Database | `DATABASE_URL` carries `sslmode=disable` on the private network, as `docs/railway.md` prescribes. |
| Legacy key | `WORKER_API_KEY` is set. It is accepted raw by the middleware and maps to the bootstrap workspace; prefer minted workspace keys and remove it once no runner uses it. |
| Trust proxy | `OPENV_TRUST_PROXY` unset, so per-IP limits (interview routes today, sign-in tomorrow) key on Railway's edge address rather than the client's. Set it to `1` behind Railway. |
| Open | SEC-5, SEC-11, SEC-14, SEC-15 are live on this deployment; SEC-1, SEC-3, SEC-6, SEC-9, SEC-16 apply in code. |

### Self-hosted (compose)

| Aspect | State |
|---|---|
| Prod overlay | Forces `POSTGRES_PASSWORD`, `CORS_ORIGIN`, `WORKER_API_KEY`; unpublishes 5432; healthchecks; memory limits; nginx unprivileged. Good. |
| Base file | Dev secrets and published 5432 (SEC-4). Running it on a reachable host is the risk. |
| Hosted runners | Require the Docker socket in the API container (root-equivalent host control); containers lack hardening beyond memory/CPU (SEC-2); `docker/docker` module vulnerable (SEC-7). Prefer the runner pool, which needs no socket. |
| TLS | Not provided by the stack; a reverse proxy must terminate it and should add HSTS. |
| Backups | Present and scripted, but unencrypted and on-host (SEC-12). |
| Open | SEC-1 … SEC-13, SEC-16 apply; SEC-14/15 depend on the operator's configuration. |

## 4. Controls verified as sound

- Passwords: bcrypt at default cost, minimum eight characters; SSO accounts
  bound to one provider, cross-provider sign-in refused, `email_verified`
  required.
- Tokens: worker keys, run tokens, pairing codes, invite tokens and session
  tokens are 32 random bytes, stored as SHA-256, shown once; env, pool and
  metrics keys compared in constant time.
- Authorisation: `requireProjectRole` / `requireOrgRole` / `requireRunAccess`
  applied on every non-public handler; every object addressed by id is
  resolved to its project or workspace first; workers cannot reach another
  org; pool key reaches pool endpoints only; run tokens scoped to one project
  and revoked at finish.
- OIDC: full ID-token verification, nonce replay binding, one-shot state
  cookie. Cookies `HttpOnly`, `Secure` under flag, correct `SameSite=None`
  pairing.
- Data: parameterised SQL throughout; LIKE escaped; cursor ids validated; git
  invoked by argv; agent slugs regex-validated with a path-escape check;
  attachment names sanitised (TC-23).
- Tenancy: search, events, SSE and notifications filtered to accessible
  projects / the authenticated user; shared products sanitised, session-only,
  attributable and removable (TC-14).
- Errors sanitised; no `InsecureSkipVerify`; connector refuses non-HTTPS
  pairing; provider settings store the key's env *name*, never the key;
  login records redacted; worker and frontend images non-root; base images
  pinned; CI promotion green-only with minimal permissions.

## 5. Prioritised actions

1. **SEC-1** — explicit tool allowlists for every agent; no auto-approved
   edits or workspace-write for agents that read interview, repository or
   web content; interviewer read-only plus `record_candidate_need`.
2. **SEC-3** — allowlist `api_key_env` to the provider catalog (or drop it).
3. **SEC-11** — fix the nginx `add_header` inheritance (repeat the headers
   in each location or use `include`), add headers in the Go API, add HSTS,
   tighten the CSP.
4. **SEC-5 / SEC-15** — throttle sign-in and registration; add a switch to
   close registration; set `OPENV_TRUST_PROXY=1` on Railway.
5. **SEC-14** — set `OPENV_METRICS_TOKEN` on the Railway API service.
6. **SEC-6** — `MaxBytesReader` on uploads and bodies; SVG as attachment
   with nosniff and a sandbox CSP.
7. **SEC-2 / SEC-4 / SEC-10** — harden hosted-runner containers; refuse dev
   secrets on non-loopback; non-root API image.
8. **SEC-7 / SEC-8** — `govulncheck` and `npm audit` in CI; bump when fixes
   ship.
9. **SEC-9 / SEC-12 / SEC-13 / SEC-16** — redact tokens in logs; encrypted
   off-host backups; refuse wildcard CORS; idle expiry and password-change
   invalidation.

## 6. Recorded in the OpenV Platform project

- Hazards HAZ-1 … HAZ-16 under **Security → Security hazards**.
- Draft requirements REQ-90 … REQ-100 under **Security**, derived from the
  new need NEED-12 (*Run it myself without an operations team*).
- Test case TC-48 *Production hardening probe* with a **fail** recorded in
  test run *2026-09-06 Assessment evidence* (steps 1, 2 and 4 failed; 3
  passed).

artifacts.title: Assistant response latency assessment 2026-09-07
artifacts.body:
Question: how much of an assistant reply is the model thinking versus everything else between Enter and the reply? Source: docs/assessments/2026-09-07-agent-latency.md.

Path of one V&V Assistant turn: the API stores the message, builds the prompt (rules, product profile, up to 12 KB of wizard state, the last 40 transcript messages) and enqueues an agent run (8–70 ms); a runner polls the queue every 2 s and claims it (0.2–1.5 s); workspace preparation (~10 ms); `claude -p` with the OpenV MCP server attached runs the model and exits; the runner posts the finish and the API appends the reply and broadcasts it over SSE (milliseconds). Nothing streams to the panel while the model writes.

Measured on one phone session against the leased pool runner (seven turns, effort low, provider claude-code): Enter to reply 14.1–20.8 s, of which everything outside the CLI was 0.3–1.6 s (about 5 %). Timed headless CLI runs put the CLI's own boot at about 1.5 s, the OpenV MCP server (67 tools listed) adding nothing measurable. That leaves 11–18 s of model time per reply, about 90 % of the wait, driven by the prompt size resent every turn and any tool round trips.

Fixes in order of payoff: (1) stream the reply text the runner already ships every 750 ms instead of showing it at finish; (2) send less prompt — resume the CLI session or trim state and transcript; (3) choose a smaller model for chat turns (maintainer decision on quality); (4) debounce wizard nudges, three of the seven turns, and answer messages sent while a turn runs; (5) poll faster or long-poll for interview-priority runs; (6) keep a CLI session warm. Instrumentation shipped with the assessment: the runner now records duration_ms, duration_api_ms and num_turns from the CLI in each run's usage log entry and its finished log line, so the split is exact per run from the next release.

artifacts.title: Report export quality assessment 2026-09-12
artifacts.body:
Scope: the document-style downloads — the **PDF specification**, the **Word document**, and the **V&V status PDF** — with the Excel, CSV and ReqIF downloads checked for the same defects where they apply. Code at `master` `41e684a`. Prompted by the maintainer's experience: the files open without error in their applications, but the formatting is poor, tables run across page breaks, images are missing, and links are broken. Method: every renderer was read end to end (`internal/domain/reports/report.go`, `docx_report.go`, `vv_report.go`, `internal/domain/downloads/download.go`, `internal/domain/exports/`); then the documents were **rendered and measured** rather than judged from code. A saved snapshot of the live OpenV Platform project (`docs/exports/openv-platform-2026-09-07.json`, 241 artifacts, 251 links) was loaded through the same `buildReportPDF` / `buildReportDOCX` / `buildVVReportPDF` / `RenderExport` entry points the download handler calls, with one added "torture" requirement that carries every markdown feature the editor accepts (GFM table, code fence, numbered and nested lists, task list, external link, `#REQ-6` and `#REQ-999-FIG-1` citations, Greek, CJK and arrow characters) plus PNG, JPEG, WebP and SVG figures. The PDFs were rasterised and inspected page by page and their text, links, drawings and images measured with PyMuPDF; the DOCX package was opened with python-docx and its XML counted. LibreOffice was not usable in the session, so Word pagination is assessed from the OOXML (which is decisive for the points made here: a table with no `cantSplit` or `tblHeader` splits and drops its header in every word processor) rather than from a screenshot. **Headline: the two documents are not the same specification, and neither is one a reader could hand to an auditor.** The PDF silently drops every description or heading whose prose is longer than a page (all four assessments in the live project are absent from it), fails outright when a project holds a WebP or SVG figure, and draws almost every artifact's table border through the artifact that follows it. The Word document contains no figures, no hyperlinks, no bullets and no page numbers, and its tables carry no keep-together or repeat-header properties. Both flatten the markdown the editor renders (tables, lists, code, links) to plain text, and the PDF loses every character outside Windows-1252. ## 1. How a download is produced There is **one shared preparation path and no intermediate document format**. Every format is rendered straight from the same in-memory snapshot; nothing is produced as HTML or Markdown and then converted. ```mermaid flowchart LR W[Download wizard
format + selection] --> H[GET /projects/{id}/download/{format}
download_handlers.go] H --> D[downloads.Download
download.go:161] D --> L[LoadReportExport
live export JSON or baseline snapshot
report.go:232] L --> S[exports.ProjectExport
artifacts · links · attachments · profile] S --> A[exports.Apply
sections · types · headings · attachment categories
selection.go:175] A --> J[JSON
export.go:257] A --> C[CSV
export.go:323] A --> X[XLSX excelize
excel.go:85] A --> R[ReqIF encoding/xml
reqif.go:317] A --> M[buildReportModel
tree · section numbers · qualified titles · link groups
report.go:162] M --> P[PDF gofpdf
buildReportPDF report.go:341] M --> O[DOCX hand-written OOXML
buildReportDOCX docx_report.go:21] P --> Z{attachment
category ticked?} O --> Z Z -- yes --> B[zip: document + attachments/
download.go:250] Z -- no --> F[file] S -.-> V[V&V PDF gofpdf
buildVVReportPDF vv_report.go:113
separate route /vv/report] ``` What is shared, and what is not: | Layer | Shared by | What it does | |---|---|---| | Snapshot | all six formats and the V&V PDF | `exports.ProjectExport`: the live export JSON, or a baseline's stored snapshot. The same struct the JSON download serialises. | | Selection | all six formats | `exports.Apply` narrows artifacts, links and attachment metadata once, so "no headings" means the same thing in a PDF and a CSV (REQ-56). | | Report model | PDF and DOCX only | `buildReportModel`: parent/child tree, `SectionNumbers`, `qualifiedTitle` ("1.2 Background" / "REQ-12 Title"), deduplicated link groups per artifact. | | Text | PDF, DOCX and the V&V PDF | `stripMarkdown` (`report.go:37`): a chain of regular expressions that deletes markdown syntax and returns one plain string. This is the whole "conversion". | | Layout | nothing | The PDF is imperative gofpdf drawing; the DOCX is string-concatenated WordprocessingML; the XLSX is excelize calls. No template, stylesheet, HTML, print CSS or document AST exists. | The consequence for quality is structural: because the body text is reduced to a string before either renderer sees it, neither renderer can produce a table, a list, a code block, emphasis, a hyperlink or an inline figure, and every fix made in one renderer has to be made again in the other. ## 2. Findings Severity: **High** = content is lost or the download fails; **Medium** = the document is materially misleading or unusable for its purpose; **Low** = polish or process. | ID | Sev. | Format | Finding | Evidence | |---|---|---|---|---| | EXP-1 | **High** | PDF | **Long prose is dropped.** A description or heading whose body does not fit on one page is routed to the "split" path, which renders only the title for headings and nothing at all for descriptions. The body and any figures vanish with no marker. | `report.go:661-700` (`renderArtifactContentWithSplitting` handles only the details-table types). DSC-1, DSC-2, DSC-3 and DSC-4 (8.7–15.8 k characters each) are absent from the rendered PDF; a probe phrase from each is not in the extracted text. | | EXP-2 | **High** | PDF | **A WebP, SVG, TIFF or BMP figure fails the whole download.** Uploads accept those types; gofpdf supports JPG, PNG and GIF only and latches an error on the document when asked to register anything else. The renderer checks `info == nil` and continues, but `pdf.Output` returns the latched error, so the handler answers 500 "failed to build download". | Allowlist `internal/api/handlers.go:2452-2463`; `report.go:1137-1140`, `:1285-1288`, `:386`. Reproduced: one WebP attachment → `unsupported image type: webp`, 0 bytes; one SVG → `unsupported image type: svg+xml`. A missing file is skipped correctly. | | EXP-3 | **High** | DOCX | **The Word document contains no images.** The renderer never emits `w:drawing`; the package has no `word/media/` part and its relationships name only `styles.xml`. The wizard describes this format as "the same specification as a .docx". | `docx_report.go:21-115`, rels `:361`; rendered package parts: `[Content_Types].xml`, `_rels/.rels`, `word/_rels/document.xml.rels`, `word/styles.xml`, `word/document.xml` — 0 drawings, 0 media. `downloadSelection.ts:38-41`. | | EXP-4 | **High** | PDF | **Table borders are drawn through the next artifact.** The outer rectangle of every details table is sized by `calculateArtifactDetailsTableHeight`, which still adds 4 mm per line of a pretty-printed attributes JSON for a row whose renderer was commented out. Prioritised actions 1. **Stop losing content (EXP-1, EXP-2).** In the split path, render heading and description bodies with `MultiCell` under auto page break instead of skipping them. Decode WebP with `golang.org/x/image/webp` and BMP/TIFF with `x/image` to PNG in memory and register via `RegisterImageOptionsReader`; rasterise SVG (`oksvg` + `rasterx`) or, failing that, print a placeholder line naming the figure. Never let a figure fail the download; clear or check `pdf.Err()` after every image call. 2. **Fix the border geometry (EXP-4).** Delete the attributes block from `calculateArtifactDetailsTableHeight` (or render the row, see 6), and draw the outer rectangle after the content from the real end position. Re-measure: the blank-page and heading-inside-border counts above are the acceptance numbers. 3. **Put a document model between the text and the renderers (EXP-5, EXP-6).** Parse bodies once with `goldmark` (GFM, in the Go ecosystem) into blocks — paragraph, heading, list (ordered/unordered, nesting), table, code, quote, with inline runs for emphasis, code, links and `#REF` citations — and have both renderers walk that tree. This replaces `stripMarkdown`, gives the DOCX real tables/lists/hyperlinks and the PDF real lists/tables/link annotations, and means the two documents finally agree with each other and with the SPA. Resolve `#REQ-12` to an internal link and `[text](url)` to an external one in both formats. 4. **Make the Word document whole (EXP-3, EXP-9, EXP-10).** Add `word/media/*` parts with `w:drawing` inline pictures scaled to the text width; `w:hyperlink` + `w:bookmarkStart` per artifact; `numbering.xml` with bullet and decimal definitions; `cantSplit` on rows, `tblHeader` on header rows, `keepNext` on labels; a footer with `PAGE` / `NUMPAGES` fields and a `TOC \o "1-3"` field; `docProps/core.xml`. Consider adopting a maintained OOXML library rather than growing the string-builder. 5. **Give the PDF a real typeface and furniture (EXP-7, EXP-8, EXP-10).** Embed a UTF-8 TrueType font (DejaVu Sans or Noto) via `AddUTF8Font`, drop the cp1252 translator, and apply the same font in link rows. Add `Bookmark` per heading, `SetTitle`/`SetAuthor`, a footer with page numbers via `AliasNbPages`, and a caption line "Figure REQ-17-FIG-1 — original.png" under each image sized to the column width (35 mm is a thumbnail, not a figure). 6. **Show V&V status and attributes (EXP-11).** Render the attribute rows the details table already has room for: priority, status, verification method and status, and typed attributes by their definitions. This closes REQ-6's open clause. 7. **Determinism and consistency (EXP-12, EXP-13).** Sort link types and targets before rendering; use one table renderer for both the fitted and split cases. 8. **Tests and documentation (EXP-16).** Turn the harness used here into a suite: render the docs export fixture and assert page count bounds, headings-inside-borders = 0, every artifact's body probe present, every figure present in both formats, no `.`-substitution for a non-Latin probe, byte-identical repeat renders. Document the `/download/*` routes in `docs/api-spec.md`. Actions 1, 2 and 7 are small, local changes to `report.go`. Actions 3 to 5 are one piece of design work and will replace most of the two renderers; doing 3 first is what makes 4 and 5 tractable. ## 6. Recorded in the OpenV Platform project - **DSC-6** *Report export quality assessment 2026-09-12* under **HDG-16 Assessments** holds this report. - Draft requirements under **HDG-3 Requirements Management Core**, derived from **NEED-7** (audit-ready traceability): **REQ-124** *Rendered document fidelity*, **REQ-125** *Figures in rendered documents*, **REQ-126** *Links and navigation in rendered documents*, **REQ-127** *Document pagination and completeness*, **REQ-128** *Character coverage and deterministic rendering*. - **TC-66** *Rendered document fidelity suite* under **HDG-14 Functional**, verifying the five, with a **fail** recorded in test run *2026-09-12 Export quality assessment*; TC-55 and TC-13 recorded as **pass** in the same run from `go test ./internal/domain/{exports,downloads,reports}/`. - Comments on REQ-6 (V&V status clause not met; its verified mark rests on tests that do not read document content), REQ-50 and REQ-52 (figure and reference behaviour stops at the SPA). - Baseline *2026-09-12 Report export quality assessment*.

artifacts.title: Bring-your-own-AI runners
artifacts.body: Each member shall be able to run agents through their own vendor CLI subscription, on their own machine (personal runner) or on a runner leased to that member alone (transient runner). The platform shall drive every consumer subscription through the vendor's own CLI, signed in by the member who owns it, and shall never share a member's subscription with another member, proxy its credentials, or execute it in the API server.

artifacts.title: First-refusal routing
artifacts.body: A run launched by a member with an online personal runner shall be reserved for that runner for a grace window (default 60 seconds, workspace-tunable) before hosted or workspace runners may claim it; ownerless runs shall route immediately.

artifacts.title: Token-only hosted runners
artifacts.body: Company-wide AI shall run in platform-provisioned hosted containers using org API tokens supplied as container environment at provision time only; provider keys shall never be stored.

artifacts.title: On-demand Agent Connector
artifacts.body: The system shall provide a downloadable Agent Connector for Windows and for Linux as a single self-contained executable. The connector shall register an openv-connector:// protocol handler. The connector shall unpack its runner components beside itself on first run. The connector shall start the member's personal runner on demand from the browser. The connector shall remember one pairing per workspace, and pairing a new workspace shall keep existing pairings valid. The connector shall start against the pairing of the workspace the browser requests. On macOS the system shall document the manual runner setup until a prebuilt connector ships.

artifacts.title: Credential-free pairing links
artifacts.body: The browser shall hand the connector a single open-or-pair link carrying the workspace and a one-time pairing code (10-minute TTL, single use). The connector shall use its existing pairing for that workspace when present and spend the code to pair only when it has none, so routine opens never rotate a working runner key; deliberate re-pairing (key rotation) remains an explicit action in workspace runner settings.

artifacts.title: Remote MCP workspace connector
artifacts.body:
The platform shall expose its tool surface over an authenticated remote MCP endpoint, so a member can attach a compliant AI client to their workspace without installing a local binary or holding a long-lived shared secret.

The endpoint shall reuse the platform's existing tool definitions and authorization rules, shall authenticate the member rather than a workspace-wide key, and shall record the member's consent per client. Not yet implemented: the local stdio path remains the supported route.

artifacts.title: Transient runner leasing
artifacts.body: The system shall lease one pre-warmed runner from its runner pool to a requesting member. The system shall reserve that runner for the leasing member alone. The system shall route runs that member launches to the leased runner on the same first-refusal terms as a personal runner. The member shall install no software to obtain or use the leased runner.

artifacts.title: Browser-relayed sign-in on a leased runner
artifacts.body:
The system shall relay each vendor CLI sign-in that runs on a leased runner to the requesting member's browser. The system shall present the authorization link the CLI produces. The system shall accept the authorization code or redirect address the member returns.

Where a vendor CLI refuses to begin a sign-in until the caller names an authentication mode, the system shall name the mode that sign-in drives. The CLI shall then produce its authorization link rather than an error. The system shall let a mode the member configured for that CLI take precedence over the one the system names.

Where a vendor withdraws a CLI sign-in from a class of accounts, the system shall state that restriction beside the sign-in before the member starts it. The system shall name the authentication route that vendor still serves.

artifacts.title: Runner lease expiry
artifacts.body: The system shall end a runner lease when the workspace's configured lease lifetime elapses. The system shall also end the lease when the leased runner claims no work within the workspace's configured idle window. Whichever condition occurs first shall end the lease, and the system shall record which one did.

artifacts.title: Run failure classification and retry
artifacts.body: The system shall classify every failed run as one of provider unavailable, authentication, workspace, timeout, agent error or worker error, and shall treat a defined subset of those classes as retryable. The system shall automatically enqueue a fresh attempt for a retryable failure of a top-level run, recording its provenance, until a configurable attempt cap is reached, and shall not auto-retry an orchestrated child run or when the operator disables auto-retry. A member shall be able to retry a terminal failed run by hand. The system shall fail a run whose heartbeat lapses and shall refuse a second terminal report for the same run. Cancelling a queued run shall cancel it atomically; cancelling a running run shall set a flag the runner honours at its next check.

artifacts.title: Run reproducibility snapshot
artifacts.body: At launch the system shall capture, on the run record, the agent definition, provider, model, effort, tool allowlist and prompt the run will execute with, so that a later reader can see exactly what a run was given even after the agent definition changes.

artifacts.title: Repository connections and per-member paths
artifacts.body: A project owner shall connect one or more code repositories to a project by URL, and each member shall record the local checkout path of that repository on their own machine. A personal runner shall operate on the member's local checkout; a leased runner shall clone the connection's URL because it holds no checkout; a hosted runner shall refuse the run. The system shall never store repository credentials.

artifacts.title: Public landing page at the root path
artifacts.body: The system shall present a public landing page at the root path to a visitor without a session, and shall route a visitor with a session from the root path to the project list. The landing page shall describe what the platform does, shall link to the manual, the source repository and the sign-in and registration screens, and shall render without a session on phone and desktop screen widths.

artifacts.title: Hosting terms stated on the landing page
artifacts.body: The landing page shall state the hosting terms in force. It shall present the hosted service as four tiers: Single User, Business Lite, Business and Enterprise. It shall describe Single User as free, with agents on the member's own AI subscription. It shall describe Business Lite as higher cloud-runner limits, agents on the workspace's own API keys, and always-on agents. It shall describe Business as shared company workspaces, teams and per-project access. It shall describe Enterprise as deployment on the customer's own servers with support, SSO/OIDC setup, custom integrations and a support SLA. It shall mark each tier that the maintainer has not released as "Coming soon" and shall show no price for that tier. It shall state that every workspace has every tier's features free while the platform is in alpha. It shall state that self-hosting is free without time limit under the Elastic License 2.0. It shall state in plain language that the licence permits self-hosting at any scale, reading and modifying the source, and paid installation or support. It shall state in plain language that the licence forbids offering OpenV to third parties as a hosted or managed service. It shall state that hosting is free without time limit for registered charities and open-source projects. It shall state the runner limits of the free tier and of Business Lite as configured in the platform's plan defaults. It shall state that agent runs use the member's own AI subscription or the workspace's own API keys, and that hosted runners do not reach code repositories.

artifacts.title: Export and import independent of plan
artifacts.body: The system shall keep project export in every supported format and project import available to every workspace regardless of the workspace's plan, and shall never condition either on payment. The landing page shall state this commitment and shall list the supported export and import formats.

artifacts.title: Public paths reachable without a session
artifacts.body: The system shall serve the root path, the pricing path, the manual and interview invitation pages to a visitor without a session, and shall not redirect a visitor away from any of these paths when an unauthenticated API call fails.

artifacts.title: Open-source tier publishes the latest baseline
artifacts.body: The platform shall provide an open-source plan for workspaces, and for every project of a workspace on that plan the system shall publish the project's latest baseline on a public open-source page and at a public address, readable without an account. The system shall not publish a project's live state or a project that has no baseline, and it shall answer a request for a project outside an open-source workspace with the same not-found response as for an unknown project.

artifacts.title: Storefront pages and demo videos
artifacts.body: The public site shall consist of the landing page and, reachable from its header and footer without a session, a page explaining how the platform works with diagrams, a page carrying five narrated demo videos served from the platform's own origin, of which two shall show the platform on a phone, a page of security and subscription-tier questions and answers, the open-source projects page, and pages for customer stories and white papers. Every page shall share one header and footer, shall fit a phone-width screen without horizontal scrolling, and its copy shall address a prospective customer in the voice of the product.

artifacts.title: Confirmed prices on the pricing page
artifacts.body: The system shall publish the plans for sale at a public path. The system shall publish each plan's confirmed amount per currency at that path. The system shall serve that path from the reading it last confirmed with the billing provider. The system shall make no request to the billing provider to serve that path. The system shall confirm each price's interval and billing scheme against the provider before it publishes the price. The system shall keep the last confirmed reading when a later confirmation fails. The pricing page shall show a confirmed amount for a tier the system prices, in place of that tier's unpriced copy. The pricing page shall show its unpriced copy in full when the operator configures no billing provider. The system shall take every displayed amount from the billing provider's confirmed reading.

artifacts.title: Tier limits for workspaces created after the announced date
artifacts.body:
The platform shall keep every workspace on the alpha terms while the operator configures no grandfather date.

The platform shall, at every boot with a grandfather date, write the alpha terms into the own limits of every workspace created before that date.

The platform shall mark each such workspace grandfathered in the same step.

The platform shall include soft-deleted workspaces in the grandfather step.

The platform shall keep a limit the workspace already sets when it writes the alpha terms.

The platform shall change no row on a second run of the grandfather step.

The platform shall refuse to boot when the grandfather step fails.

The platform shall, with a grandfather date, cap the free tier at two members, one shared workspace per creator, and 300 leased cloud-runner minutes per calendar month.

The platform shall include hosted automation in the Business Lite plan.

The platform shall include teams, per-project team access and the workspace budget in the Business plan.

The platform shall never cap the members of a plan billed per seat.

The platform shall name the Billing tab in every limit refusal on a hosted deployment.

Rationale: the announcement is a promise made in public; enforcing it through the same data the enforcement reads makes it mechanical rather than a code path.

artifacts.title: Read-only workspace over its plan, with export always available
artifacts.body:
The platform shall refuse every mutating request scoped to a workspace that holds more members or projects than its plan allows, with the code plan_read_only and a remedy.

The platform shall allow removing a member, leaving, revoking an invitation, deleting a project, deleting the workspace, the billing endpoints and import on such a workspace.

The platform shall serve every read on such a workspace.

The platform shall serve export in every format on such a workspace.

The platform shall never delete data because a workspace is over its plan.

The platform shall report the read-only state and the limits exceeded in the workspace limits response.

Rationale: a lapsed trial cannot mint a permanent free team, and nobody's work is ever held hostage.

artifacts.title: Coverage computation
artifacts.body: The system shall compute verification coverage of requirements (via verifies links) and validation coverage of user needs (via validates links), including latest test-run results.

artifacts.title: Traceability matrix
artifacts.body: The system shall present a traceability matrix relating needs, requirements and test cases.

artifacts.title: Gap reporting
artifacts.body: The system shall report unverified requirements, unvalidated needs and failing verifications as actionable gaps.

artifacts.title: Test run recording
artifacts.body: The system shall record test runs capturing pass/fail results per test case over time.

artifacts.title: Change impact analysis
artifacts.body: The system shall report the set of artifacts a change to a given artifact affects by traversing its traceability links upstream, downstream or in both directions, grouped by artifact type and annotated with the link path that reached each one. The system shall bound the traversal at a fixed depth so that a cyclic graph terminates.

artifacts.title: Agent-executed test runs
artifacts.body: The system shall let a project editor hand the automated test cases of a test run to an agent, and shall build the agent's instruction naming exactly those test cases. Each test case shall carry an execution method of automated, manual or physical. The system shall withhold manual and physical test cases from the agent's instruction and shall refuse, with a forbidden response, any result an agent run records against one. The system shall stamp every agent-recorded result with the run that produced it and shall show that provenance beside the result. A result applied from an approved proposal shall count as human-executed.

artifacts.title: Agent-drafted test cases
artifacts.body: The system shall let a project editor select requirements and launch the seeded test-case author agent against them. The agent shall run in proposal mode, so that every drafted test case and its verifies link reach the project only through human approval.

artifacts.title: Guided product definition wizard
artifacts.body: The system shall provide a step-by-step guided wizard (framing, personas, needs, requirements, NFRs, hazards, verification stubs, review) that materializes traceable draft artifacts as the user progresses. Hazards shall be captured under risk categories (Safety, Technical, Security, Programme, Operational) and non-functional requirements under quality attributes (Performance, Reliability, Usability, Security, Maintainability, Regulatory). Materialized artifacts shall be organized under automatically created section headings — one per wizard step, with a sub-heading per used NFR category, per used hazard category, and per verification grouping (Functional first, then each quality attribute stubbed) — reused across wizard re-runs within the same session. A category shall place an artifact in the document rather than appear as a prefix on its title, and a verification stub shall be filed beside the kind of requirement it verifies, carrying the same title as that requirement. A category the wizard no longer offers shall file its artifact directly under the step's own heading rather than create a section no step can refill. Once any guided session exists for a project, the wizard's navigation entry shall be hidden; the wizard is then reached only via the Product Overview page's adaptive control (Start / Resume / Modify guided definition).

artifacts.title: Interview invitation links
artifacts.body: Members shall be able to invite internal or external people by link to an interview session; invitees shall need no OpenV account.

artifacts.title: Conversational AI elicitation
artifacts.body: The interview session shall be an AI-led natural conversation that asks questions to understand what the invitee needs from the product, and shall record proposed artifacts as interview-tagged drafts for member review - never as directly approved content.

artifacts.title: Random test product generation
artifacts.body: The new-project flow shall offer a testing mode that generates a random product concept (name, description, vision, problem statement, target users) across varied categories including software, hardware, games, toys, and appliances, with the option to reroll, and shall seed the guided definition wizard with the generated framing so the connected V&V Assistant can expand it into a full definition.

artifacts.title: Agent-invented demo products
artifacts.body: The new-project flow shall let a member invent a demo product with their own connected agent, briefed with worked examples and the invariants the built-in concepts hold to, and shall offer the result as a roll tagged as the agent's. A reply that misses those invariants shall buy one retry told exactly what to fix; anything still below the standard shall be shown to its inventor but kept out of the collection everyone rolls from. Inventions shall be kept in the browser and mixed into later rerolls.

artifacts.title: Shared demo-product pool
artifacts.body: The system shall maintain one community pool of demo products that every workspace reads and contributes to, so the roll list grows across tenants rather than going stale per browser; a roll shall mix built-in concepts, this browser's inventions and the pool, deduplicated so no product rolls twice as often as its neighbours. Reading shall require a session. Publishing shall require a signed-in person — agent run tokens and worker keys shall be refused — and an invention shall publish automatically under its inventor's own session, so every entry stays attributable to an account. Entries shall be flattened server-side to inert single-line text carrying no line breaks, backticks, angle brackets, links or agent-suggestion markers, capped per field, deduplicated by name, limited per workspace per day and capped in total. Responses shall carry no author identity.

artifacts.title: Community pool moderation and takedown
artifacts.body: Because nothing reviews a shared demo product before other tenants see it, the system shall let any signed-in user report an entry, shall hide an entry once three distinct people have reported it, and shall let a platform admin delete one outright; repeated reports from one account shall count once. Author identity shall be stored for rate limiting and takedown only. Before anyone shares, the wizard shall state that publication is public and permanent, that rolls tagged with the globe were written by other users, and that creating a project from a product never shares it.

artifacts.title: V&V Assistant across the wizard and artifact notes
artifacts.body:
The system shall provide one assistant, named the V&V Assistant, reachable both beside the guided definition wizard and in the Notes panel of the requirements module. One conversation shall serve a whole project, so that what a member asks in the wizard is present in the notes and the reverse. The Notes panel shall present the artifact's comments and the assistant as separate tabs, and shall offer the assistant whether or not an artifact is selected. With an artifact selected, that artifact shall be supplied to the turn as fenced untrusted content, so the assistant answers about what the reader has open and cites it by its stable reference.

The system shall supply every turn with the project's outline as fenced untrusted content, beside the wizard and beside the project alike. The outline shall list each artifact's reference, type, title and place in the tree, in document order. The turn shall name the project and tell the assistant to read an artifact in full with its tools before proposing a change to its text. Beside the wizard, the turn shall also carry the wizard's state, and shall tell the assistant that an entry carrying an artifact id is already an artifact, to change with a change or move card rather than a replacement. Suggestion cards shall apply in the wizard to the entry sections they fill. Beside the project, suggestion cards shall apply to the project itself. Beside the project, the system shall add a wizard-shaped suggestion as a draft artifact under the standard heading for its kind. The assistant shall propose a new artifact of any catalogue type at a named place. The assistant shall propose a change to a named artifact's title, body or attributes. The assistant shall propose a move of a named artifact under a heading or among its siblings. The system shall accept a card that changes the project in the wizard and beside the project alike, and shall apply it to the project. An artifact shall be nameable by its reference or by its id. A change shall alter only the fields it names. A change shall merge attributes over the existing ones. A move shall never place an artifact inside its own subtree. A move shall require its anchor to sit under the destination. A move shall renumber the sibling group. The person shall apply each card with a click. The assistant shall not write to the project itself. The new-artifact, change and move cards shall be a gated feature. The gated feature shall reach a stable-channel workspace with its next stable release. A gated workspace shall receive a description of the change instead of a card.

A session created solely to hold the conversation shall not count as a guided definition in progress, so that opening the notes chat neither removes the wizard from the project navigation nor offers to resume a definition nobody started.

A workspace provisioned before the assistant was named shall adopt the current name, description and system prompt for its seeded agent, field by field and only where the workspace still carries the text the previous seed wrote; a field a member has edited shall be left as they wrote it, and an agent already current shall not be rewritten. The agent's slug shall not change, so that a workspace provisioned before the rename keeps a working chat.

artifacts.title: Votes on shared demo products
artifacts.body: A signed-in member shall be able to vote once for a shared demo product and shall be able to withdraw that vote. The system shall show each product's vote count and its votes from the last 7 days. The random-product picker shall offer three filters. The first filter shall pick at random from the whole visible pool. The second filter shall list the five products with the highest all-time vote count. The third filter shall list the five products with the highest vote count over the last 7 days. The system shall exclude a hidden product from every list and from voting. A runner key shall hold no vote. The system shall add a starter set of shared demo products when it starts. The system shall add no duplicate of a starter product on a later start. The system shall keep a product a member has published under the same name as a starter product. While the shared pool holds at least one product, the picker shall offer only products from that pool.

artifacts.title: Streamed assistant replies and coalesced wizard nudges
artifacts.body: While an assistant turn runs, the system shall show the reply text in the chat panel as the model writes it, and shall replace the growing text with the final message when the run finishes. The runner shall report the text written so far at most once per second, and the system shall forward it to the session's stream at most twice per second per run. Where a vendor CLI emits no incremental text, the system shall show the reply only when the run finishes and shall document that limit. While an assistant turn for a guided session is in flight, the system shall hold the latest wizard nudge instead of launching a second turn, and shall launch exactly one turn with that nudge when the running turn finishes.

artifacts.title: Notification history, flags and views
artifacts.body: A member shall be able to clear every notification in their inbox. The system shall keep a cleared notification and shall show it in the cleared view. The system shall count only uncleared notifications towards the unread badge. A member shall be able to flag and unflag any of their own notifications. The system shall show every flagged notification in the flagged view, whether or not the member has cleared it. The system shall keep a notification flagged when the member clears it. A member shall be able to delete their cleared notifications permanently. The system shall read a member's notifications only for that member. The system shall page each view in blocks, and shall return each notification exactly once across the pages of one view.

artifacts.title: Claim routing suite
artifacts.body: Automated suite plus live check: a personal key never claims another user's run; reserved runs return no-content to workspace workers during the grace window and are claimable after hosted_after expires; ownerless runs route immediately.

artifacts.title: Shared demo-product pool suite

artifacts.body:
Go suite over the MCP tool table: create_baseline, get_vv_coverage (lean projection by default, full report on detail), get_vv_gaps, close_test_run (only completed/aborted reach the API) and record_test_result (evidence is a list of attachment IDs, so a bare string is wrapped and the API stops rejecting the body); every tool surfaces API errors; the openv-mcp entrypoint prefers a run token, accepts a workspace runner key, and refuses to start with neither.

Pass criterion: every test passes in `go test ./internal/mcp/...`.

artifacts.title: Wizard section filing suite

artifacts.title: Activity log naming suite

artifacts.title: V&V Assistant notes chat suite
artifacts.body:
Client suite over the session helpers that decide where the conversation lives: a session created only to hold the chat is told apart from a wizard someone worked on (by step, answers and status), a project with only chat-created sessions reports no wizard progress, and the newest session is the one the notes panel reads so it shows the transcript the wizard resumes into. Paired with the Go prompt tests that fence the artifact on screen.

Project cards (DES-52): `internal/api/guided_copilot_prompt_test.go` — a project-mode turn fences the outline after the trust rules with an injected title inside the fence, offers the artifact/edit/move shapes, carries no wizard-state fence and no longer forbids changing artifacts; a wizard turn carries both the state fence and the outline, is offered the three shapes, tells the assistant that a locked entry's artifact_id cannot be replaced and maps to an artifact, and names the project and get_artifact for reading full text; a wizard turn with no outline (a listing that failed) offers no project shapes; a gated workspace is offered none of the three shapes and is told they arrive with the next stable release while still seeing the outline; `renderProjectOutline` follows the tree (children indented under parents in sort order, a stale parent promoting its children), cuts to budget in document order saying how many it left out, and reads "no artifacts" for an empty project. `frontend/src/utils/artifactOrder.test.ts` — placement by anchor, by first/last, under another heading (last by default, beside a sibling, or to the root), refusing an anchor under another heading, a move into its own subtree, and a move that changes nothing; sibling order and the next free slot. `suggestionDrafts.test.ts` — an artifact of any catalogue type placed by reference with normalised references, an unknown type and a title-less artifact refused, an edit read as only the fields it names, an empty edit and an emptied title refused, a move read by parent, anchor or position, a move that says nowhere or contradicts itself refused. `applySuggestion.test.ts` (mocked API) — an edit sends only the named fields with attributes merged over the current ones, an artifact id is accepted where a reference is expected, an unknown reference is explained; a move reparents and renumbers only what changed, reorders by anchor, refuses a move under itself and explains an anchor elsewhere; a placed artifact is created as a draft last under the named heading, or placed after the named sibling with the group renumbered; a later card in a batch can move what an earlier card created. `GuidedChatPanel.test.tsx` — project cards are labelled Apply change / Move / + Add to project with their summaries beside the project, the wizard is offered the same cards with the same labels and never "+ Add to wizard" for them, and an applied key shows the card as done.

Manual: the layout audit's `notes-assistant` screen (the three cards beside the requirements module) and `guided-assistant` (the same cards beside the wizard) across `android,iphone,desktop`, with the rendered pages read to confirm the cards' labels and summaries.

Pass criterion: every test passes in `go test ./cmd/... ./internal/...` and `npm test` in `frontend/`, and the audit reports no finding for `notes-assistant` or `guided-assistant`.

artifacts.title: Quality rules editor presentation
artifacts.body: Frontend Jest suite over the quality rules editor at both levels: each severity select offers the four severities exactly once with no separate inherit entry, and opens on the value the level is in force with; a project select opens on the workspace's value unflagged; changing it away from the workspace value shows an override warning naming that value, and choosing the workspace value again clears the warning and drops the override, so a save sends only the severities that differ; the convention list offers each convention once with the inherited one preselected, and a project convention that differs from the workspace's carries the same warning.

artifacts.title: Figure numbering and version suite
artifacts.body: Go suite over the figure reference rules: a reference formats and parses round-trip, a non-figure (an artifact reference, a zero or missing number, a filename) is refused, the stored filename is the figure's with the uploaded extension carried over, an upload with no usable extension gets none, and a hostile extension (quotes, backslashes, path traversal, percent escapes, an over-long tail) is stripped rather than carried into a filename or a Content-Disposition header. A new attachment starts at version one carrying no figure until the repository allocates one.

artifacts.title: Description reference suite
artifacts.body:
Client suite over the reference helpers and the rendered description (`frontend/src/components/artifactReferences.test.ts`, `frontend/src/components/ArtifactBody.test.tsx`).

1. The single-hash offer lists an artifact's own figures before the artifacts it links to, excludes anything it is not linked to, follows a link in either direction and names each neighbour once, skips a neighbour with no reference to cite and figures belonging to other artifacts, and offers nothing while an artifact is still being created.
2. The double-hash offer lists figures from every artifact, this artifact's first, names the artifact each other figure belongs to, offers no artifacts at all, and needs no link to the artifact holding the figure.
3. The caret rules: a hash opens the offer only at a word boundary (so 'PR#12' and URL fragments are ignored), it closes once the writer moves past it, and it reads from the caret rather than the end of the text. Two hashes are read as the project scope; three or more are not a marker at all.
4. Insertion replaces what was typed, keeps the text that followed, leaves the caret after the reference, and writes back the marker that was typed.
5. Rewriting for the renderer links a citation of either marker, keeps the marker in the link's text and out of its target, links every citation in a body, leaves a markdown heading of any level and a hash inside a word alone, and keeps trailing punctuation out of the link.
6. Rendered: a citation's anchor carries the reference scheme rather than an empty target, never opens in a new tab, and hands the bare reference to the application with the browser's own navigation prevented. An ordinary link still goes through the renderer's URL sanitiser and still opens in a new tab. Without a handler, citations render as plain text rather than as links that do nothing.

Pass: every assertion holds, and step 6 fails when the reference scheme is not carried through the renderer's URL sanitiser.

artifacts.title: Artifact drag placement suite
artifacts.body: Client suite over the drag helpers: the pointer's quadrant resolves to before/after/child and is read relative to the row rather than the page, a zero-height row does not divide by zero, an artifact is recognised as its own descendant to any depth, a cycle already in the data terminates the search rather than hanging, and a planned move places a sibling before or after, appends a child last, moves an artifact out to the root or between two different parents, and refuses a drop onto itself, into its own subtree, or one that changes nothing.

artifacts.title: Project menu group expansion suite
artifacts.body: Client suite over the helpers that decide which menu groups are open: an unchosen group is collapsed, the group holding the current page opens itself, an explicit choice beats both defaults, and one click closes a group that opened itself. The route helper reads the module out of a project path (including a deep path and the overview) and reports nothing outside the project. Stored choices round-trip through browser storage, and stored junk — unparseable text, an array, a non-boolean value — falls back to the default rather than breaking the menu.

artifacts.title: Download selection and archive suite
artifacts.body:
Go suite over the selection filter and the download assembly, plus the client suite over the form that drives them.

Selection: the whole project passes through untouched; headings drop out on request; a section brings its whole subtree including grandchildren; a type filter and a section filter combine; a link survives only when both of its ends do; attachment metadata always travels with its artifact while the files are opt-in; a parent cycle already in the data terminates rather than hanging; the snapshot handed in is never mutated.

Assembly: every format renders the same narrowed snapshot; the baseline's name reaches the renderer; a download with no attachment categories is the plain file; one with categories is a zip holding the document and the files; only the categories asked for are packed; an unreadable file is recorded in a manifest rather than failing the download; archive entry names cannot climb out of the archive; two files with one name both survive.

Options: sections, types and attachment categories are counted off the project, and a project with none offers none.

Client: everything ticked sends no filter, an unticked box sends the narrowing, the query carries a baseline but not the live project, and an empty selection is refused before it is sent.

artifacts.title: Runner lease lifecycle suite
artifacts.body: Domain and repository suites over the pool: leasing takes an idle node and mints one credential handed over exactly once; a second lease for the same member returns the first; a one-node pool refuses a second member; the atomic lease under eight concurrent callers gives four nodes to four callers and never the same node twice; the sweep ends leases past their hard expiry, past their idle window, stuck starting, and on nodes that stopped heartbeating, with the reason recorded on each; activity defers the idle timeout; extending is capped from the lease's start.

artifacts.title: Headless sign-in relay suite
artifacts.body: Automated: the loopback replay forwards the pasted path and query to the CLI's own advertised listener, ignores any host named in the paste, rejects a paste carrying no authorization code with a message naming what to paste, and reports a rejected replay rather than swallowing it; ANSI-painted terminal output is reduced to text the authorization URL can be scraped from. `internal/runner/geminicli_test.go` covers the Gemini authentication mode: the sign-in flow names `GOOGLE_GENAI_USE_GCA=true` alongside `NO_BROWSER=1`, a run names the same mode with its isolated settings path and its run token intact when nothing else names one, and a run whose own or inherited environment names an API key, Vertex, or a gateway base URL is left alone. artifacts.title: Review queue journey and status suite

artifacts.title: Seed adoption updates only unedited fields
artifacts.body:
Automated, `internal/seeds` (`TestAdoptSeedDefaults*`).

1. An agent holding a previous release's prompt and tools, with the current name and description, adopts the new prompt and the newly granted tools; a field the workspace owns (model) is left alone.

artifacts.title: Side panel open state across the three modes
artifacts.body:
Automated, `frontend/src/components/panelMode.test.ts`.

1. A pinned panel is open whether or not the pointer is over it, and whatever the reveal says.
2. An auto-hiding panel opens on hover and closes without it.
3. A hidden panel does not open on hover.

Pass: all cases hold.

artifacts.title: Mobile journey suite
artifacts.body: Playwright projects: Desktop Chrome (every spec), WebKit (the smoke and landing journeys), iPhone 13 (WebKit engine, touch) and Pixel 5 (Chromium, touch), the last two running `e2e/tests/mobile.spec.ts` only. The mobile journey: the landing page and pricing section fit a phone; register on a phone-sized screen; create a project and land in the compact shell (menu button present, no permanent sidebar); open the drawer, expand a group and navigate, and see the drawer close on arrival; in the requirements module see the Tree / Document / Notes control, create a requirement from the tree pane, tap it and land on its document, switch to Notes and back with the tree state kept; return to the project list; open both settings pages and reach their last tab. artifacts.title: Email verification pipeline
artifacts.body:
Automated (CI): `internal/domain/users` — Register is verified with the policy off and pending with it on; SSO accounts verified; a reissued link kills the previous one; confirm is single use; an expired link is refused; a corrected address is applied only on confirm and refused when taken at issue or at confirm. `internal/notify` — policy from env (no host, off switch, enabled), link building and rendering, bounded send (success, failure, hang). `internal/api` — register sends one mail carrying `/verify-email?token=` and still answers 200 when the mail fails, and sends nothing with the policy off; confirm 200/400/409; resend 401 without a cookie, 415 without a JSON body, 409 when verified, 202 with `sent_to`, 429 after the burst, 502 when the mail fails, 409 on an issue conflict, 400 with the policy off; change 202/400/415; `/auth/config` reports the flag; the middleware passes everyone with the policy off, answers 403 `email_unverified` to an unverified cookie session with it on, passes a verified session, never gates the open auth paths or a Bearer credential. `internal/persistence/postgres` (needs `OPENV_TEST_DATABASE_URL`) — columns round-trip, a superseded link is dead, consume is single use, an expired link is refused, a taken address rolls back leaving the account unverified, the 0024 backfill verifies SSO rows and not password rows. Frontend Jest — the wall shows the address and the four actions, resend calls the API and starts the cooldown, a corrected address is sent, a verified account redirects to projects, no session redirects to sign in, `?token=` calls confirm. The Playwright suites run with no SMTP and stay unchanged.

Manual, on the local stack with an SMTP sink on 127.0.0.1:1025 and the API started with `OPENV_SMTP_HOST=127.0.0.1 OPENV_SMTP_PORT=1025 OPENV_SMTP_FROM=openv@localhost`: the boot log says verification is required; register through the API → the response says `email_verified: false` and the sink receives a mail with a `/verify-email?token=` link; a request to `/api/v1/projects` with the session cookie → 403 `email_unverified`; POST the token to `/auth/verify-email` → the user comes back verified; `/api/v1/projects` → 200; resend four times → the fourth is 429 with `Retry-After`; change to a taken address → 409; stop the sink and resend → 502; restart with `OPENV_EMAIL_VERIFICATION=off` → a fresh registration is verified at once and `/auth/config` reports the flag off. In the browser, registration lands on the Check your inbox page and the emailed link lands on the app.

artifacts.title: Vulnerability gate run
artifacts.body: Inspection of the CI pipeline plus one run of the gate. 1. `.github/workflows/ci.yml` carries a job that runs `govulncheck` over `./cmd/... ./internal/...` and `npm audit --omit=dev --audit-level=high` in `frontend/` on every pull request, and neither step is marked continue-on-error. 2. `make vuln` (or the two commands directly) on the current head: govulncheck exits 0 and reports no reachable vulnerability; npm audit exits 0 with no high or critical advisory in production dependencies. 3. The job appears among the check runs on the pull request's head commit and its conclusion is success. Pass criterion: all three hold. A reachable high-severity finding fails the run, which is the gate working, not a test failure of this case; record it as fail with the advisory ID and open the fix.

artifacts.title: Vendor translation suite: model, effort and run timeout
artifacts.body:
Verifies REQ-82's vendor-translation clauses: that each CLI adapter renders the agent's model, reasoning effort and timeout in that vendor's own terms, and that no vendor default silently displaces the agent's own bound.

**Method.** Automated, Go unit tests over the adapters' argv builders in `internal/runner` (`go test ./internal/runner/...`), plus direct execution of the pinned vendor binary to confirm the flags and value formats the adapters emit are the ones the CLI actually accepts.

**Steps and expected results**

1. **Model.** Build argv for an agent naming a catalogued model. The vendor's model flag carries that model verbatim.
2. **Effort.** Build argv across the full effort vocabulary. An effort the vendor lacks maps to its nearest tier — for Antigravity, three rungs, with `xhigh` and `max` capping to `high` — and an effort the vendor cannot express is omitted rather than guessed.
3. **Timeout, set.** Build argv for an agent whose `timeout_seconds` exceeds the vendor CLI's own non-interactive default. The vendor's timeout flag is present and carries the agent's value, so the agent's timeout is what ends the run. For Antigravity this is `--print-timeout`, whose default is 5m0s against a default agent timeout of 1800s.
4. **Timeout, unset.** Build argv for an agent with no timeout of its own. No timeout flag is emitted — neither an empty value, which fails to parse, nor a zero, which would end the run immediately.
5. **Value format.** Execute the pinned vendor binary with the emitted timeout value. The CLI parses it and exits 0.
6. **No auto-approval.** For every trust setting, argv never carries the vendor's approve-everything flag (`--dangerously-skip-permissions`, `--yolo`).

**Pass criterion.** Every step as expected, for every adapter in the registry that expresses the property in question.

artifacts.title: Figure restore suite
artifacts.body:
Verifies REQ-50's restore clauses.

**Method.** Automated. Go over the repository against a real Postgres (`internal/persistence/postgres`, `OPENV_TEST_DATABASE_URL`); Jest over the history entry's description.

**Steps and expected results**

*The round trip (`TestRestoreVersion`)*

1. Build a figure with three versions: v1 an image and a title, v2 a different image and name, v3 a rename over v2's image. Restore v1.
2. The restore writes **v4**, not v1 — a restore moves forward.
3. v4 carries v1's file **and** v1's title. A restore that brought back the drawing under v3's name would show one figure under another's.
4. v4 records who performed it, and records `restored_from = 1`.
5. The figure itself now reads v4, with v1's file path, title and file size.
6. The history holds **four** versions, newest first. Nothing was deleted.
7. v2 is still retrievable and still points at its own file — the superseded drawing a requirement may have been reviewed against is intact.

*Refusals (`TestRestoreVersionRefusals`)*

8. Restoring the version the figure already shows returns `ErrAlreadyCurrent` (409 at the API).
9. Restoring a version the figure never had returns `ErrNoSuchVersion` (404).
10. Restoring on a figure that does not exist returns `ErrNoSuchVersion`.
11. After all three refusals the figure is still at v1 — a refused restore writes nothing.

*The history entry (`frontend/src/components/ImageGallery.test.tsx`)*

12. A version with `restored_from` reads "restored from vN".
13. It still reads as a restore when the restored image is the one already showing — where comparing file paths alone would call it a rename.
14. A version without `restored_from` is unaffected: upload, rename and new image read as before.

**Not covered.** The browser round trip — the *Restore* control, its confirmation, the 409 message, the gallery refreshing behind the dialog, and the `figure-revert` gate hiding the control — needs a running stack.

**Pass criterion.** Steps 1-14 as expected.

6. `OverPlan` names only counts past their ceiling: at the ceiling is not over, a resource limit is not a count, no reading is never over.

artifacts.title: Lean agent context
artifacts.body: Agents shall obtain project requirements context from the requirements database and the kanban card history through tools. A prompt the system builds for an agent shall carry only bounded and fenced content. That content shall consist of the product profile, the wizard state up to 12 kilobytes, the last 40 transcript messages and the artifact on screen. The system shall place no whole requirement document in an agent prompt.

artifacts.title: Solo Founder
