artifacts.body: Defines and builds products end-to-end alone. Uses OpenV as product manager, requirements tool and virtual development team, with AI agents doing the heavy lifting under their review.

artifacts.title: Company Admin
artifacts.body: Owns a company workspace: manages members, teams, project access, workspace AI keys and the hosted runner. Accountable for tenant privacy and spend.

artifacts.title: Team Contributor
artifacts.body: Engineer or product person working in granted projects. Brings their own AI subscription via a personal runner; launches and reviews agent work.

artifacts.title: External Stakeholder
artifacts.body: Customer, domain expert or colleague invited by link to express needs in a natural conversation. Has no OpenV account and never sees the tool itself.

artifacts.title: GUI-editable agent definitions
artifacts.body: Agents shall be defined as markdown files that are fully editable in the GUI and synchronizable from disk.

artifacts.title: Proposal-gated writes
artifacts.body: By default the system shall divert every agent-initiated change to project data into a proposal. Such a change shall take effect only after a person approves the proposal. A workspace admin shall be able to set an individual agent to direct write mode. The system shall record that choice in the agent definition. A write made with a workspace runner key shall land directly, as REQ-42 states, because the key holder is the person acting.

artifacts.title: User-composable crews
artifacts.body: Users shall compose multi-agent architectures using an org-chart editor (department groups, hierarchical layout) and a network-diagram editor; a default crew shall ship with each workspace; crews shall accept human members with employees/agents/all views.

artifacts.title: Unified kanban
artifacts.body: A kanban board shall track work items for both AI agents and human workers, including agent handoffs to humans.

artifacts.title: Manual, scheduled and triggered automation
artifacts.body: Agent utilization shall be launchable manually, on cron schedules, and on project events (triggers).

artifacts.title: Code repository operation
artifacts.body: Agents shall optionally operate on connected code repositories in addition to OpenV data.

artifacts.title: Tool-surface access for maintenance sessions
artifacts.body:
The MCP tool server shall authenticate with any credential the API already accepts for the operations it performs - an agent run token injected by a platform-launched run, or a workspace runner key - so that agent sessions outside a platform run reach project data through the same tool surface as platform runs, rather than through bespoke API scripts.

The presented credential, not the tool server, shall determine what the session may read and write: a run token stays scoped to its run's project and its agent's write mode, while a workspace runner key carries workspace-wide editor rights and no proposal gating.

artifacts.title: Maintenance loop covered by tools
artifacts.body:
The tool surface shall cover every step of the requirements-maintenance loop an agent performs in session: reading project data, editing artifacts and links, recording verification evidence, reporting verification coverage and traceability gaps, and capturing baselines. No maintenance step shall require an agent to bypass the tool surface with raw API calls.

Bulk project export is excluded by design: it is a file-level backup operation, and exposing it as a tool would invite agents to pull a whole project into context against the lean-context rule.

artifacts.title: Seed updates reach unedited agents only
artifacts.body: When a platform release changes a seeded agent definition, the system shall update an existing workspace agent field by field, and shall update a field only where that field still holds the exact value written by a previous release of the same seed. The system shall preserve every field a workspace member has changed.

artifacts.title: Locking an agent against automatic updates
artifacts.body: The system shall let a workspace administrator lock an individual agent, and shall exclude a locked agent from every automatic seed update, regardless of whether the agent's fields still match a previous release of the seed. The system shall keep the lock state in the agent's definition file as well as in the agent registry, shall show the lock state in the agent list and the agent editor, and shall return a locked agent to automatic updates when an administrator removes the lock.

artifacts.title: Recovering a hidden side panel
artifacts.body:
The system shall let a reader set each side panel to pinned, auto-hiding or hidden. The system shall leave an edge strip in place of a panel that is not pinned. The system shall open the panel when the reader clicks that strip, including a panel the reader has hidden. The system shall keep the opened panel visible until the reader dismisses it. The system shall open an auto-hiding panel on hover. The system shall leave a hidden panel shut on hover.

The system shall present that edge strip as a control the reader can see without hovering it. The system shall let the reader operate that strip from the keyboard. The system shall give that strip a name that says which panel it opens.

The system shall keep a panel on screen while the reader changes that panel's state. The control that changes the state shall stay where the reader is pointing until the reader dismisses the panel.

artifacts.title: In-app and email notifications
artifacts.body: The system shall notify a member in the application when a proposal awaits their review, when a run they launched fails, when an interview they created completes, when an artifact enters review in a project they edit, when someone mentions them in a comment, when a review is requested of them, and when a workspace budget threshold is reached. The system shall push a new notification live to the member's open sessions, shall never notify a member of their own action, and shall let each member read notifications, mark them read and opt out of email. When an operator configures a mail transport, the system shall also email the high-signal types; otherwise the system shall send no email and shall not fail.

artifacts.title: Proposal review controls
artifacts.body: The system shall let a project editor approve or reject proposals one at a time or in bulk. The system shall cap the proposals one run may raise at a fixed number and shall refuse further proposals from that run once the cap is reached. A run shall be able to name a not-yet-approved artifact proposal by a temporary reference so that a link proposal in the same run resolves to the real artifact when both are approved, and the system shall fail the link proposal when the artifact proposal is rejected or approved after it. A run that finishes with pending proposals shall await approval and shall succeed or fail only when its last proposal is resolved.

artifacts.title: Crew templates and portability
artifacts.body: The system shall ship built-in crew templates that instantiate against a workspace's seeded agents, shall let a member clone a crew, and shall export a crew as a portable document and import one into another workspace. An export shall carry agents by slug and shall omit human members; an import shall skip a node whose agent slug the target workspace lacks together with its edges, and shall refuse a document of the wrong kind or without a name.

artifacts.title: Board-driven agent runs
artifacts.body: Moving a board card into a column owned by an agent shall enqueue a run of that agent for the card, and the run's progress and outcome shall be written to the card's activity feed. A crew hand-off to a human member shall create a board card assigned to that member instead of launching a run.

artifacts.title: Agent model, effort and tool allowlist
artifacts.body: Each agent definition shall name its provider, its model chosen from a catalog or typed freely, an optional reasoning effort, an allowlist of the tools it may use, a turn cap and a timeout. The runner shall pass the model and effort to the vendor CLI in that vendor's own terms, mapping an effort the vendor lacks to its nearest tier and omitting one it cannot express. Where a vendor CLI applies a bound of its own to a non-interactive run, the runner shall pass the agent's timeout to that CLI. The agent's timeout shall be the limit that ends the run. The runner shall grant an agent only the tools on its allowlist. A workspace admin shall set each provider's authentication mode and default model, and a runner shall report the CLIs, sign-in state and models it detects on its host.

artifacts.title: AI context surface
artifacts.body: The system shall render a project as a compact outline map, one line per artifact carrying its stable reference, title, non-draft status and inline link annotations, and shall serve the map both as an agent tool and as an API endpoint. The system shall render the map from a named baseline on request, stamped with the baseline's name and capture time. The system shall serve a one-call context bundle for an artifact addressed by reference or identifier, holding its body, ancestor path, children and every linked artifact with an excerpt. Every tool that takes an artifact identifier shall also accept its stable reference.

artifacts.title: Hierarchical versioned modules
artifacts.body:
The system shall organize artifacts as hierarchical, ordered modules within projects, with parent/child structure and stable ordering. Creating an artifact relative to another — before it or after it — shall place the new artifact in that position within its sibling group rather than at the end of the group.

Dragging an artifact onto another shall both reorder and re-parent, decided by where the pointer is released: the upper half shall place it before that artifact, the lower left after it, and the lower right shall make it a child of it. The artifact under the pointer shall show which of the three would happen before the drop is made. An artifact shall never be droppable into its own subtree, and a drop that would change nothing shall be refused rather than written. A drop into a collapsed artifact shall expand it, so the moved artifact remains visible.

artifacts.title: Typed artifacts with attributes
artifacts.body: The system shall support typed artifacts (persona, user need, requirement, design item, test case, hazard, heading, description and other), each carrying free-form attributes and, where the workspace or project defines them, typed attributes validated on write.

artifacts.title: Semantically constrained links
artifacts.body: The system shall enforce link-type rules: verifies (test case to requirement), validates (test case to user need), satisfies (design item to requirement), derives-from (requirement to user need), decomposes-to (requirement to requirement), mitigates (design item to hazard), impacts (any artifact to any artifact) and relates-to (any artifact to any artifact, bidirectional). The system shall reject a link whose end types the rule for its type does not allow, with an error naming the rule.

artifacts.title: Artifact version history
artifacts.body: Every artifact edit shall create a retrievable version, and any prior version shall be restorable.

artifacts.title: Project baselines
artifacts.body: The system shall capture immutable named baselines of a project's full artifact and link state.

artifacts.title: Project download in every format
artifacts.body:
The system shall offer one download action per project, from which a member chooses the output format. The system shall render a project as a PDF specification, a Word document, an Excel workbook, structured JSON, a CSV table and a ReqIF interchange file. The PDF and the Word document shall include V&V status. The Excel workbook shall carry one sheet per artifact type, a links sheet and a project cover, with the same columns as the CSV table plus each artifact's reference and section number. The JSON shall carry everything a project import restores.

The system shall prepare one project snapshot per download and render every format from that snapshot, so that the same request yields the same content in whichever format a member chose. The system shall download a baseline's snapshot in place of the live project when the member has selected a baseline.

artifacts.title: Visible artifact references
artifacts.body:
The system shall show each artifact's stable reference wherever a reader might cite it: leading the artifact detail heading, on every non-section row of the project tree, as a Reference row in the details table, qualifying every traceability row, and titling each artifact in the PDF and DOCX reports. A section shows its document number in place of a reference.

When an edit changes an artifact's type to one with a different reference prefix, the system shall assign a new reference drawn from the new type's own counter. The system shall never reuse a retired reference number.

artifacts.title: Document section numbering
artifacts.body: The system shall number heading artifacts hierarchically (1, 1.1, 1.2, 2) from their position in document order, shall number headings only, and shall number a heading nested under a non-heading within its nearest heading ancestor. Reordering the document shall renumber it while stable references stay fixed. Numbers shall be computed rather than stored, and served only when a list request asks for them, in which case the whole project is numbered rather than the returned page.

artifacts.title: Requirement wording convention
artifacts.body:
Each workspace shall carry a requirement quality rule set: the normative convention its requirements are written in — ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148 "shall" or RFC 2119 must/should/may — and the severity, including off, of each wording rule.

Each project shall inherit its workspace's rule set until it stores an override, and each level shall store only the keys it overrides, so a project that re-grades one rule keeps its workspace's convention. A workspace that has stored nothing shall resolve to the "shall" convention.

The linter shall judge wording against the resolved convention, so that a keyword binding under one convention is not reported as weak wording under the other, and shall report a keyword belonging to the other convention so that one project does not drift between the two vocabularies.

artifacts.title: Copy, paste and duplicate artifacts
artifacts.body:
The artifact context menu shall offer copy, paste before, paste after and duplicate alongside its create actions. Copying shall take an artifact's content — type, title, body and attributes — and not its identity, its links or its figures, so that a copy never asserts traceability nobody created. Pasting shall place the copy as a sibling of the artifact acted on, immediately before or after it, and duplicating shall place a copy of that artifact directly after it. A pasted artifact shall be titled so a reader can tell it from its original. Paste shall be offered but unusable until something has been copied.

The copy shall carry none of the original's version history. The system shall open the copy's feed with a single system note naming the original by its stable reference and the version copied, so that a reader can tell where the copy came from. The system shall write the note only when the copying member can read the original.

artifacts.title: Quality rules visible to people and agents
artifacts.body:
The resolved rule set shall be visible to everyone who writes requirements, human or agent.

Workspace admins shall set the house style and project editors shall set a project's override from settings. Each setting shall list every value it permits exactly once, preselected to the value in force at that level. A project setting that differs from its workspace value shall carry an override warning naming the workspace value, so that a local value is never mistaken for an inherited one.

Agents shall reach the same rules through the tool surface, and the project orientation map an agent reads before drafting shall state the convention in force, so that an agent writes to the project's house style rather than inferring one from the artifacts it happens to read.

artifacts.title: Referencing figures and artifacts in descriptions
artifacts.body:
An artifact's description shall let its author cite a figure or another artifact by typing a hash, which shall offer that artifact's own figures and the artifacts it is already linked to, filtered by what is typed, and shall insert the chosen reference into the text.

The single-hash offer shall be confined to what the artifact is already connected to, so that a citation written with one marker names a relationship the traceability matrix holds. A hash inside a word shall not open the offer, so that ordinary text such as a URL fragment is left alone.

An author shall be able to cite anything in the project by typing two hashes. That offer shall list every figure, naming the artifact each figure belongs to, and shall then list every other artifact that has a reference. It shall exclude the artifact being edited. It shall require no traceability link, because the doubled marker is what tells a reader the citation reaches outside what this artifact is connected to. A run of three or more hashes shall not open either offer, so that a markdown heading is left alone.

The two-hash offer shall name no relationship for an artifact, because there is no link to name.

The inserted reference shall retain the marker it was written with, so that a reader can tell a citation reaching outside the artifact from one that does not.

A reference in a rendered description shall be a link: following an artifact reference shall select that artifact, and following a figure reference shall open that figure, whichever artifact holds it, without leaving the description. A rendered reference shall carry the destination the application resolves, so that following one never navigates the reader to the document they are already reading. Text that merely resembles a reference — a markdown heading, a hash inside a word — shall be left as written, and trailing punctuation shall not be absorbed into the link.

A reference already written into a description shall resolve for every member, whether or not that member's workspace has received the release that introduced the marker.

A description shall preserve the line breaks its author typed.

artifacts.title: Advisory quality findings
artifacts.body:
Quality findings shall be advisory. The linter shall score an artifact and explain each finding in terms of the rule that produced it, and shall never reject, gate or divert a write, whoever the author is.

A quality report shall carry the rule set it was produced under, because the same wording scores differently between conventions and a score without its rules cannot be read.

artifacts.title: Panels that yield their space
artifacts.body:
The project navigation and the artifact notes panel shall each offer three states: pinned, auto-hidden and hidden. The reader shall choose each panel's state independently, and the system shall remember that choice per person across sessions. A pinned panel shall take its width from the page. An auto-hidden panel shall present an edge affordance that opens the panel over the document on hover, and shall leave the document's layout unchanged. A hidden panel shall leave that affordance and nothing else, so that the reader can always bring the panel back.

The requirements workspace shall fit the height of the browser window at every window size, so that the window itself never scrolls. The artifact tree, the artifact document, the notes panel and the project navigation shall each scroll within their own bounds. The toolbar shall wrap to further rows without displacing the regions below it.

artifacts.title: Named actors and entities in the activity log
artifacts.body: The activity log shall name the person, agent or runner behind each recorded event and the artifact, link, work item, baseline, comment, test result or agent run it affected, showing those names alongside the stored identifiers so the audit trail reads without resolving identifiers by hand. A name that can no longer be resolved falls back to the identifier alone.

artifacts.title: Figures change only while editing
artifacts.body: Adding, replacing and removing a figure shall be possible only while editing the artifact that carries it. A view that presents an artifact for reading shall present its figures for reading, so that what the document shows cannot change by a stray click.

artifacts.title: Numbered figures with versioned files
artifacts.body:
A file attached to an artifact shall be a figure carrying a reference of its own, formed from the artifact's stable reference and a per-artifact figure number (REQ-17-FIG-1). A figure number shall be unique and shall never be issued twice: the counter shall only move forward, so that deleting a figure does not return its number to circulation and concurrent uploads cannot be allocated the same one. An artifact carrying no stable reference shall yield no figure reference rather than one that would collide once it has one.

The system shall accept an image, a PDF or a CAD file as a figure, and shall refuse any format outside the catalogue it publishes. It shall record a figure's format from the uploaded file's extension where the catalogue names that extension, because a browser reports most CAD formats only as an unspecified byte stream. It shall check an uploaded file's leading bytes against the signature of the format its name claims, where that format has one.

The system shall classify every figure by what can be done with its bytes: an image, a document or a model. It shall report that classification with the figure, so that a client need not derive it from the format itself.

A figure's file shall be stored and served under its figure reference, so that a downloaded file is named for what the document calls it, and the name the uploaded file had shall be retained alongside it.

The system shall serve a figure inline only when it is a raster image. It shall serve every other figure as a download under a policy that permits nothing and refuses framing, so that a format able to carry script is never rendered on the platform's own origin.

The application shall show an image in place, a PDF in a reader, and an STL as a preview the reader can rotate. It shall offer every other format a statement of what it is and a download rather than an approximation of its contents. It shall offer a download for every figure whatever its format.

A member shall be able to replace a figure's file with a new version. The figure shall keep its reference, superseded versions shall remain retrievable, each version shall record who uploaded it and when, and a version may carry a different format from the one before it.

A member shall be able to restore an earlier version of a figure. A restore shall write a new version carrying that earlier version's file and its title together, and shall leave every existing version in place. The new version shall record which version it restored. The system shall refuse a restore naming a version the figure never carried, and shall refuse one naming the version the figure already shows.

A change of figure version shall take the artifact to a new version and shall write a note to the artifact's feed naming the figure and the versions it moved between. That artifact version shall not demote an approved artifact nor mark its links suspect, because the artifact's own statement is unchanged.

artifacts.title: Collapsible project menu groups
artifacts.body: The project navigation shall group its destinations under headings. The navigation shall collapse every group by default, so that each group occupies one line until the reader opens it. The navigation shall expand or collapse a group when the reader selects its heading. The system shall remember each choice per person across sessions. The navigation shall expand the group holding the reader's current page until the reader collapses that group.

artifacts.title: Choosing what a download contains
artifacts.body:
The download action shall let a member narrow what the download contains, and shall apply that choice to the prepared snapshot before rendering any format.

A member shall be able to select which top-level sections to include, and the system shall include every artifact beneath a selected section. A member shall be able to select which artifact types to include, and shall be able to exclude headings so that the download holds artifacts alone. The system shall include a traceability link only when the download contains both artifacts it joins.

A member shall be able to select which categories of attachment to include, and the system shall offer only the categories the project holds. The system shall deliver the rendered document and the selected attachment files together as one archive whenever a member selects any attachment category. The system shall name each attachment in the archive by its figure reference where it has one.

The system shall state what the current selection contains before the member commits to it. The system shall refuse a selection that matches no artifact.

artifacts.title: Artifact status workflow
artifacts.body: The system shall carry each artifact through the statuses draft, in review, approved and superseded, and shall accept only these transitions: draft to in review, in review to draft, in review to approved, and approved to superseded. The system shall refuse any other transition. The system shall treat superseded as terminal. The system shall demote a new content version of an approved artifact to draft while the archived approved version keeps its status. Approving an artifact shall clear the suspect flag on every link that touches it.

artifacts.title: Suspect links and the review queue
artifacts.body: The system shall mark a traceability link suspect when the content of either artifact it joins changes after the link was made, and shall keep the link suspect until a project editor confirms it. The system shall present a review queue per project that lists every suspect link and every artifact in review, so that a reviewer finds all pending review work in one place. The system shall not mark a link suspect for an attribute-only change or a figure version change.

artifacts.title: Baseline comparison
artifacts.body: The system shall compare a baseline against another baseline or against the live project, and shall report the artifacts and links added, modified and removed between the two. For a modified artifact the system shall name which fields changed and shall show the old and the new value. The system shall treat a link that was recreated with a new identifier but the same ends and type as unchanged.

artifacts.title: Artifact search
artifacts.body: The system shall let a member search artifact titles and bodies by text across every project the member can access in the active workspace, and shall return only artifacts from projects the member holds at least viewer access to. The system shall use an index-assisted search where the database supports it and shall fall back to a sequential search where it does not, with identical results.

artifacts.title: Semantic search and duplicate detection
artifacts.body: When an operator configures an embedding provider, the system shall compute a vector embedding for each artifact's title and body, shall re-embed an artifact only when its content or the embedding model changes, and shall offer nearest-neighbour search and duplicate-candidate detection over those embeddings per project. When no embedding provider is configured the system shall behave as if the capability did not exist, and shall make no outbound call. An embedding failure shall never fail the artifact write that triggered it.

artifacts.title: Typed attribute definitions
artifacts.body: The system shall let a workspace admin define custom artifact attributes for the workspace and a project editor define them for one project, each with a name, a type of text, number, date or enumeration, an optional list of permitted values, and the artifact types it applies to. The system shall validate an artifact's attribute values against the definitions in force for its project on every write, and shall reject a value of the wrong type or outside the permitted list. A project definition shall take precedence over a workspace definition of the same name.

artifacts.title: Project import
artifacts.body: The system shall create a project from an OpenV JSON export or from a ReqIF interchange document. The system shall assign fresh identifiers at version one to every imported artifact, shall reconstruct the parent hierarchy, links, status and attributes, and shall preserve each artifact's stable reference. The system shall reject a malformed document, or an enumerated attribute value outside its declared values, with a validation error rather than a partial import. The system shall carry attachment metadata but not attachment files across an import.

artifacts.title: Project templates
artifacts.body: The system shall let a project editor save a project as a workspace template, and shall let any member create a new project from a built-in or workspace template. A workspace template shall be visible only inside its workspace.

artifacts.title: Rendered document fidelity
artifacts.body:
The system shall render an artifact body in the PDF specification and the Word document with the same structure the artifact editor shows: paragraphs, headings, ordered and unordered lists with their numbers and nesting, tables, code blocks with their indentation, block quotes, and emphasis, inline code and strikethrough runs. The system shall render the same body identically in the PDF and the Word document, so that a reader of either sees the same specification.

The system shall show, for every non-heading artifact in both documents, its priority, status, verification method and verification status where set, and each typed attribute by its definition's label.

artifacts.title: Figures in rendered documents
artifacts.body:
The system shall embed every image figure attached to an included artifact in both the PDF specification and the Word document, placed after that artifact's body, scaled to the width of the text column and no taller than half a page, and captioned with the figure's reference and its name, so that a citation such as REQ-17-FIG-1 in a body can be matched to the picture it names.

The system shall not place a figure that is not an image into a rendered document. A document or a model has no depiction to embed, and printing a statement of that in the body of a specification would tell a reader less than omitting it. Such a figure shall remain citable from a body, and its file shall still be available through a download that includes attachments.

The system shall render a figure of every image type an upload accepts, converting or rasterising a type the document format cannot embed directly. Where an image figure cannot be rendered the system shall print a placeholder line naming the figure and its reason, and shall never fail the download because of a figure.

A download that groups attachments by kind shall group a figure by its format rather than by its having a figure number, so that a document or a model is not offered as a figure.

artifacts.title: Links and navigation in rendered documents
artifacts.body:
The system shall render every traceability row, every artifact reference cited in a body and every figure reference cited in a body as a link that leads to that artifact or figure within the same document, in both the PDF specification and the Word document. The system shall render a markdown link in a body as a link that opens its URL and shall keep the URL in the document.

The system shall give each document a cover block naming the project and the snapshot, a table of contents built from the headings, a running page number on every page, and a document outline that a viewer's navigation pane reads. The system shall set the document's title and author metadata.

artifacts.title: Document pagination and completeness
artifacts.body:
The system shall include every artifact the selection contains in the rendered PDF specification and Word document, including a heading or description whose body is longer than one page, and shall never omit content because of its length.

The system shall draw each artifact's table so that its border encloses exactly its own rows and never crosses another artifact. The system shall keep a table row on one page, shall repeat a table's header row on every page the table continues onto, shall keep a heading or a table label on the same page as the content that follows it, and shall render one artifact's table with the same layout whether or not it crosses a page.

artifacts.title: Character coverage and deterministic rendering
artifacts.body:
The system shall render every character of the Latin, Greek and Cyrillic scripts that an artifact title or body contains in the PDF specification and the V&V status PDF from an embedded font, and shall carry every Unicode character an artifact holds into the Word document unchanged, so that a reader's word processor renders it with its own fonts. Where the PDF's embedded font has no glyph for a character the system shall print a placeholder glyph rather than drop or transliterate the character.

The system shall render the same snapshot with the same selection to the same document content on every request, apart from the generation timestamp, so that two downloads of one baseline compare equal.

artifacts.title: Workspace logo on document covers
artifacts.body:
A workspace admin shall be able to upload a logo for the workspace as a PNG, JPEG, GIF or WebP image of at most 2 MiB, replace it, and remove it. The system shall serve the logo to workspace members and shall refuse a file whose declared type or content is not one of those image types.

The system shall print the workspace logo and the workspace name at the top of the first page of the PDF specification and the Word document for every project in that workspace, and shall render the documents without them when no logo is set or the file cannot be read.

artifacts.title: Source statement on rendered documents
artifacts.body: The PDF specification and the Word document shall state on their first page which of two sources they were rendered from: a baseline, named with the baseline's name, its unique identifier and the time it was captured; or the live project, named with the export time and a sentence that it is not a baseline. The system shall repeat the project name, the baseline name or the export time, and the page number of the total on every page, and shall write the project name, the author and the source statement into the file's document properties.

artifacts.title: Document templates, field and evidence choices
artifacts.body:
The download action shall let a member start a PDF specification or Word document from a named template and shall offer at least the presets Specification, Requirements review, Test planning and Verification & Validation, each setting the artifact types kept and the content carried. A member shall be able to change any choice a template made, and the document shall record on its cover the template it started from.

A member shall be able to switch on or off, independently: the table of contents; traceability rows under each artifact; embedded figures; each requirement's verification rollup with the coverage summary and gap lists; and the latest test result per test case with a test-run appendix. A member shall be able to choose which attribute fields, standard or custom, each artifact shows, and the system shall offer only the fields the project's artifacts carry, with a count for each.

The system shall apply the same choices whether they arrive from the download wizard or as request parameters, and an explicit parameter shall take precedence over the template.

artifacts.title: Uploaded profile picture
artifacts.body:
A signed-in user shall be able to upload a profile picture for their own account, replace it, and remove it. The system shall accept a PNG, JPEG, GIF or WebP image of 2 MiB or smaller, and shall refuse a file whose declared type or content is not one of those image types.

The system shall serve the uploaded picture to signed-in users and shall show it wherever the account is shown: member lists, crew nodes and the account menu. The system shall draw every profile picture as a circle of fixed size that keeps its shape beside a long name.

While the account holds an uploaded picture, the system shall keep it in place of the picture an identity provider supplies at sign-in. When the user removes the uploaded picture, the system shall take the identity provider's picture again at the next sign-in.

artifacts.title: Release notification and customer-facing release notes
artifacts.body:
The system shall notify every account once when the released version of the platform changes. The notification shall name the release and shall carry the customer-facing notes of that release. The system shall show the full release history to a signed-in user on a What's new page.

The system shall identify each release by a semantic version. The system shall derive that version from the notes of the release. A release carrying a new feature shall raise the minor version. A release carrying only maintenance updates and fixes shall raise the patch version. The major version shall rise only when the operator declares the release a major one. The first numbered release shall be 0.1.0. The system shall keep each date-named release that preceded semantic versioning under the name the platform announced it with.

The system shall group the notes of a release under New features, Maintenance updates and Bug fixes. The build pipeline shall refuse a release note that names none of those three groups. The notification and the What's new page shall present the notes under the group the pull request filed each in.

The system shall serve the parsed releases. The system shall not serve the release notes source file, which also holds notes for work that has not shipped and guidance written for contributors.

An open tab shall detect a newer release behind the same address within 10 minutes, or when the tab returns to view, and shall offer a reload.

Each pull request shall add at least one customer-facing release note for the change it makes. The build pipeline shall refuse a pull request that adds none, unless the pull request carries the label that marks it invisible to users. The release pipeline shall refuse a release whose notes name nothing newer than the release already deployed.

artifacts.title: Release channels and cadence
artifacts.body:
The platform shall offer two release channels on the shared service: nightly and stable. A nightly release shall be every promotion of a green master that carries new release notes, and shall be versioned as REQ-143 defines (a semantic version derived from the notes: 0.2.0, 0.2.1). A stable release shall not be a separate build or version: on the first working day of each month, the platform shall designate as the stable release the newest release that has served the nightly channel for at least 7 days and is newer than the current stable release, by a marker line under that release's heading in the release notes. A fix release shall be designated the same way from the newest release without the 7-day soak when the maintainer asks for it.

Once the staging environment exists, the platform shall promote a nightly release automatically at 03:00 UTC on every day that master is green and carries new release notes.

artifacts.title: Release channel by plan
artifacts.body:
The platform shall place every Personal and Lite workspace on the nightly channel, and shall not allow those workspaces to change channel. The platform shall place a Business workspace on the stable channel by default and shall allow its admins to move it to the nightly channel. The platform shall place an Enterprise workspace on the stable channel by default, and shall offer an Enterprise customer a dedicated instance pinned to a stable release instead.

The platform shall show a workspace's channel and its current release in workspace settings.

artifacts.title: One build, features gated by channel
artifacts.body:
The shared service shall run one build for every workspace. The platform shall switch on a new feature for a nightly-channel workspace at the release that carries it, and for a stable-channel workspace at the workspace's upgrade time for the first stable release that is that release or a later one. The platform shall deliver maintenance updates, bug fixes and security fixes to every workspace at the next nightly release, regardless of channel.

A pull request that adds a new feature shall put that feature behind a channel gate keyed on the release it ships in, and shall file its release note under New features; maintenance updates and bug fixes shall be filed under their own groups and shall not be gated.

artifacts.title: Upgrade window chosen by the workspace
artifacts.body:
A Business or Enterprise workspace admin shall be able to choose the day of the month and the hour, in the workspace's time zone, at which each stable release turns on for the workspace, up to 14 days after the release is designated stable. The platform shall keep the previous stable behaviour for the workspace until that time. The platform shall notify the workspace's admins when a stable release is designated, with its release notes, and again 24 hours before it turns on for the workspace.

A workspace admin shall be able to turn the next stable release on early for their own account alone, to try it before the workspace moves.

artifacts.title: Dedicated instance pinning and support window
artifacts.body: A dedicated Enterprise instance shall run the stable release its customer chose and shall change release only on a date the customer chose. The customer shall be able to run the next stable release on a staging copy of their instance before the upgrade. The platform shall support a dedicated instance for 90 days after the next stable release is designated, shall warn the customer's admins 30 days and 7 days before that window closes, and shall deliver security fix releases to a dedicated instance within the window on the day they are designated.

artifacts.title: Release notes and notifications per channel
artifacts.body:
The platform shall publish the notes of a stable release as the merged notes of every release since the previous stable release, grouped as new features, maintenance updates and bug fixes. The platform shall notify the members of a nightly-channel workspace at each nightly release, and the members of a stable-channel workspace when a stable release turns on for that workspace, in each case with the notes for that release. The What's new page shall open with the workspace's own channel, shall state the workspace's current release and its next scheduled release, and shall mark which releases in the history are stable releases.

This refines the release notification in REQ-134, which today notifies every account at every release.

artifacts.title: Staging environment before nightly promotion
artifacts.body:
The platform shall run a staging environment. The release pipeline shall deploy every merge to master to staging. Staging shall use its own database and shall hold no data copied from production. Staging shall admit only the maintainers and the Enterprise customers who are previewing a release.

Each deployed service shall report the commit of the build it runs. The release pipeline shall run the automated smoke tests against staging on every merge to master. The release pipeline shall start a smoke run only once every staging service reports the commit under test.

The release pipeline shall promote a commit to the nightly channel only after that commit's automated smoke tests have passed on staging. The release pipeline shall promote a commit only after the commit's database migrations have applied to the staging database without error. The maintainer shall be able to run any release candidate on staging by hand before cutting a stable release.

Note on the first paragraph: an empty staging database exercises a schema migration but not a data migration. Staging therefore evidences that a migration applies, not that it transforms production-shaped data correctly. Closing that gap needs an anonymised restore of production, which the platform does not perform today.

artifacts.title: Security fixes reach every channel at once
artifacts.body: The platform shall deliver a security fix to every workspace on the shared service at the next nightly release, and shall cut a stable fix release carrying it on the same day, so that no channel setting or upgrade window holds a security fix back. The release notes for a security fix shall say that it is one.

artifacts.title: Semantic versioning and compatibility across stable releases
artifacts.body:
The platform shall version releases semantically, as major.minor.patch, and shall derive each version from the notes of that release (REQ-134). The HTTP API, the MCP tools, the export formats and the runner protocol shall stay backward compatible from one stable release to the next within a major version. The platform shall announce the removal of an endpoint, tool, field or format in the release notes of two consecutive stable releases before the release that removes it, and shall keep the removed item working through those two releases.

Note: this requirement originally proposed calendar versioning by year and month with no major version. Semantic versioning replaced that when the numbering shipped, so that the size of a change is visible in its number; the compatibility promise above is unchanged apart from being bounded by the major version.

artifacts.title: Project hierarchy
artifacts.body: The platform shall allow a project to name one parent project in the same workspace, shall refuse a parent that is the project itself or one of its descendants, and shall list a project's child projects. Access to the parent and to the child shall remain separate grants (REQ-16), so a supplier granted the child project sees only what it is granted on the parent.

artifacts.title: Flow-down links across projects
artifacts.body: The platform shall provide a refines link from a requirement to a requirement, which may cross from one project into another. The platform shall accept a refines link into another project from a member with editor rights on the source project and viewer rights on the target project. The platform shall include every link touching a project, from either end, in that project's link list, export, baseline, coverage, matrix and map, and shall name a linked artifact of another project with that project's name and the artifact's stable reference.

artifacts.title: Verification flow-up across projects
artifacts.body: For each requirement refined by requirements of other projects, the platform shall report those refinements with each one's verification rollup computed in its own project, and a flow-down rollup equal to the worst of them, ordered fail, blocked, unrun, uncovered, pass. A requirement with no test case or attestation of its own shall take the flow-down rollup as its rollup and shall not be reported as a gap. A requirement with evidence of its own shall report the worse of its own rollup and the flow-down. A requirement without a verification method shall remain method-missing.

artifacts.title: Artifact owners and reference parties
artifacts.body: The platform shall let every artifact carry an owner: the party or member responsible for it, held in the owner attribute and matched by name. Each project shall keep a list of reference parties it recognises as owners, with the workspace's own company always present as the first party and never removable; a project editor shall be able to add and remove the other parties. The platform shall offer the parties and the project's members when an owner is chosen, and shall filter an artifact list by owner in the interface, the API and the agent tools.

artifacts.title: Owner-filtered export
artifacts.body: Every download format shall accept a list of owners and shall then contain only the artifacts owned by them, the headings that organise them and the links among them, keeping a link to an artifact of another project. The download wizard shall offer the owners present in the project, and the export script shall accept the same owner filter and every download format.

artifacts.title: Requirement description in the document fields table
artifacts.body: In the PDF and Word documents, each artifact's fields table shall carry the artifact's description as a row after the version and before the attributes, so that the description is read with the reference and attributes rather than lost among the figures. The row shall be the only copy of the description in the artifact's section, shall keep the description's formatting (paragraphs, lists, tables, code, links and emphasis), and shall be omitted for an artifact with no description.

artifacts.title: Figure titles as tracked versions
artifacts.body:
A figure shall carry a title of its own, distinct from the filename of its upload. The system shall show a figure by its title under the figure in the gallery, in the figure history, and in the caption under the picture in PDF and Word documents. The system shall show a figure with no title by the filename of its upload.

An editor shall be able to set a figure's title, up to 255 characters, and shall be able to clear it. The system shall record each rename as a new version of the figure over the same image. Each such version shall carry the title, the member who set it and the time. The figure's history shall list every title the figure has had alongside every image it has had.

A rename shall take the artifact to a new version. The system shall write a note to the artifact's feed naming the figure, the old name and the new name. That artifact version shall not demote an approved artifact and shall not mark its links suspect. The system shall write nothing for a rename to the title the figure already has.

A figure that receives a new image shall keep its title.

artifacts.title: Runner pool load disclosed as a band
artifacts.body:
The system shall present the transient runner pool's availability to a workspace member as one of four bands: available, busy, full, or unavailable.

The system shall select the available band when more than 30 percent of the online pool nodes are idle.

The system shall select the full band when fewer than 5 percent of the online pool nodes are idle.

The system shall select the busy band at every idle share between those two thresholds.

The system shall select the unavailable band when no pool node is online.

The system shall omit the pool's node count, idle count and leased count from every response it serves to a member who does not hold the workspace-admin role.

Rationale: a member can hold only one leased runner at a time, so an exact free count is not a figure they can act on. Publishing that count to every account discloses the deployment's capacity and its current occupancy. The workspace-admin pool view retains the counts, which an operator needs in order to size the pool.

artifacts.title: To-dos by person, raised from notes
artifacts.body:
The system shall present a project's work items on a page of their own, grouped by the person each item names as its assignee. The system shall include every project member in that grouping, including a member with no open work. The system shall gather work naming an agent or a team, and work naming nobody, into groups of their own rather than omitting it. The system shall let a member restrict the page to their own work, and shall hide finished work until the member asks for it.

The system shall let a member raise a to-do from a note on an artifact. The system shall offer, as that to-do's assignee, a project member the note names with an @mention. The system shall not create a to-do from a mention alone. The system shall link a to-do raised from a note to the artifact the note is on.

The system shall show, on a note that raised a to-do, that to-do's status as it stands when the member reads the note. The system shall refuse a to-do that cites a note belonging to another project.

artifacts.title: Search by artifact ref
artifacts.body:
The system shall match a search query against artifact refs as well as titles and bodies. The system shall treat the query case-insensitively and shall ignore whitespace surrounding it, so that "req-30", "REQ-30" and " Req-30 " each name the same artifact.

The system shall rank an artifact whose ref equals the query first. The system shall rank an artifact whose longer ref merely contains the query below that exact match. The system shall likewise rank an artifact that cites the query in its body below it. The system shall return each result's ref alongside its title.

The system shall serve a query that names a ref from the keyword path whatever ranking mode the caller asked for, because nearest-neighbour ranking over embeddings does not order identifiers.

The system shall restrict ref matching to a workspace whose release channel has reached the release that introduced it, and shall search titles and bodies alone for every other workspace.

artifacts.title: Artifact history feed and its filters
artifacts.body:
The system shall present one feed for the artifact a member has open. The feed shall hold the entries the system recorded when that artifact changed. The feed shall also hold the comments members wrote on that artifact. The system shall order the feed newest first. The system shall label the feed History.

The system shall add an entry to the feed when a member saves a new version of the artifact. The system shall add an entry when a member changes its status. The system shall add an entry when a member adds or removes one of its links. The system shall add an entry when a member adds or replaces one of its figures. The system shall add an entry when a member restores an earlier version. The system shall add an entry when a run records a test result against it.

The system shall offer three filters over the feed: every entry, recorded changes alone, and comments alone. The system shall name what a filter selects whenever that filter selects no entry. The system shall keep a comment visible to its author after they write it, under every filter.

artifacts.title: Tagging people and references inside a note
artifacts.body:
A note's author shall be able to name a project member by typing an at sign. The system shall then offer the project's members. The system shall narrow that offer to match the characters the author types. The system shall insert a handle the server resolves to the chosen member. The system shall omit from the offer any member for whom no such handle exists.

A note's author shall be able to type two at signs to name a member and ask for a to-do. The system shall raise that to-do when the author posts the note. The system shall assign the to-do to the member the note names. The system shall link the to-do to the artifact holding the note. The system shall copy the note into the to-do's description.

The system shall save the note before it raises any to-do. The system shall keep the note and report the failure when it cannot raise the to-do.

The system shall continue to offer a to-do on a note the author has already posted. That offer shall let a member set the title, the person and the due date.

A note's author shall be able to cite a figure or an artifact by typing one hash or two. The system shall offer there what REQ-52 offers in a description.

The system shall render a citation in a posted note as a link to what it names. The system shall mark a named member, so a reader can tell a mention from ordinary text.

The system shall render every note as the text its author typed. The system shall interpret no other markup in a note.

The system shall restrict these offers to a workspace whose release channel has reached the release carrying them. The system shall render the tags in an existing note for every member, whatever channel their workspace follows.

artifacts.title: Quality finding for a citation with no traceability link
artifacts.body:
The quality linter shall flag an artifact that cites an artifact it holds no link to. A link in either direction shall satisfy this. That finding shall speak at error severity by default. Error is the weight the linter gives unfinished placeholder text.

The finding shall name the artifact the text cites. The finding shall ask a member to link the two artifacts.

The linter shall raise the finding for a citation written with one hash. The linter shall raise it for a citation written with two. A link a member deletes shall leave the citation behind, and the linter shall then raise the finding against it.

The linter shall raise no finding for a citation naming a figure. A figure citation makes no claim of a relationship between two artifacts.

The linter shall raise no finding for an artifact citing its own reference.

The linter shall report each cited artifact once, even when the text names it more than once.

The linter shall raise no finding when its caller has not established the artifact's links. A caller that cannot read the links shall therefore see no finding, rather than one against every citation in the artifact.

A project shall be able to set this finding's severity, down to off, as it can for every other rule.

The linter shall judge a citation by the same rule when it lints one artifact and when it lints a whole project.

artifacts.title: Project-wide review rounds
artifacts.body: The system shall let a project editor start a review round for a project. The system shall move every artifact whose status is draft to in review when a round starts. The system shall include every artifact type in a round by default, headings and descriptions included. The system shall restrict a round to the artifact types the caller names when the caller names any. The system shall leave an approved artifact approved when the round runs. The system shall leave an artifact that is already in review or superseded unchanged. The system shall record each artifact the round moves as an ordinary status change in that artifact's history. The system shall report the number of artifacts the round moved and the number it left approved. The system shall refuse a review round from a proposal-mode agent run.

artifacts.title: Stateless review rounds over the existing status machine
artifacts.body:
POST /api/v1/projects/{id}/review-round (editor; proposal-mode agent runs refused) calls artifacts.DefaultService.StartProjectReview, which walks the project's current artifacts and applies the ordinary draft to in_review transition to each in-scope draft. A round can therefore never reach a state a person could not reach one artifact at a time.

The round stores nothing — no round record, no "last reviewed" stamp. Re-running it does the right thing because the status machine already carries the signal: editing an approved artifact's type, title or body demotes the new version to draft (REQ-65), so by the time a later round runs, a changed requirement is a draft again and the round pulls it back into review, while an untouched approved artifact is still approved and is left alone. Running a round twice with nothing in between writes nothing the second time.

Default scope is every type except heading and description, which carry no claim to sign off; an explicit types list overrides it and an unknown type is a 400 before anything is written. Each move publishes artifact.status_changed and writes the same feed note a single submission would, so an artifact's own history explains how it entered review; the round additionally publishes one project.review_round_started event against the project. A per-artifact write failure is logged and skipped rather than aborting the round, so a round never stops halfway with no record of where. The response carries the moved artifacts plus already_in_review, approved, superseded and out_of_scope counts, which together account for every current artifact.

Surfaces: the Send project for review button on the Review Queue (gated on the project-review-round feature key) and the start_project_review MCP tool.

artifacts.title: Deciding a review from the review queue
artifacts.body: The system shall show each artifact in the review queue with its type, its reference and its title. The system shall show an extract of that artifact's description and a preview of each of its figures. The system shall let a project editor approve an artifact directly from the review queue. The system shall let a project editor send an artifact in review back to draft directly from the review queue. The system shall require a comment before it sends an artifact back. The system shall record that comment as a note on the artifact, resolving mentions, to-do markers and citations as it does for a note written in the notes panel. The system shall post the comment before it changes the artifact's status. The system shall leave the status unchanged when it cannot post the comment. The system shall let a reviewer select any number of artifacts in the review queue. The system shall offer a control that selects every artifact in the review queue. The system shall apply an approval or a send-back to every selected artifact. The system shall report the number of artifacts it failed to decide. The system shall leave those artifacts in the review queue.

artifacts.title: Review decisions on the queue, over the ordinary status and note writes
artifacts.body:
The review queue's In review section is a table: checkbox, artifact summary (type chip, ref, linked title, a flattened extract of the markdown body), a figure strip, and per-row Approve / Send back. Figures come from GET /api/v1/projects/{id}/attachments, grouped client-side; an image is an img thumbnail, any other kind a chip naming it, both linking to the file. The figure fetch is best-effort: a failure costs the previews, never the queue.

No decision endpoint was added. Approve is PUT /api/v1/artifacts/{id}/status with approved; send back is a note followed by the same call with draft. A decision made here is therefore the same write as one made on the artifact, lands in the same history, and needs no second authorization path.

Rejection order is load-bearing: the note is posted FIRST, then the status moves. If the note fails nothing has been rejected and the reviewer retries; the reverse order can leave an author with work back in draft and no word on what was wrong with it, which is the one outcome a rejection must not produce.

The reason is written in NoteComposer, extracted from ChatterPanel so the notes panel and the rejection dialog share one implementation: same @ / @@ / # / ## menus, and the same postNote() write, which creates the chatter entry (the server resolves @ mentions into notifications from it) and raises a to-do for each @@ target. A second implementation would have drifted, and the second one would have been the one quietly lacking mentions.

Bulk actions act on the selection: approve fires the transitions concurrently and counts refusals; send back opens one dialog and posts the one reason on each artifact in turn. Either way, what could not be decided is reported and stays in the table.

Gated on the review-queue-decisions feature key; a workspace without it keeps the previous plain list, because the statuses and notes the controls write are ordinary and must stay readable everywhere.

artifacts.title: Stepping between artifacts while reading
artifacts.body:
The requirements workspace shall offer a control that steps to the previous artifact and a control that steps to the next artifact. The workspace shall state the artifact's position in the reading sequence and the length of that sequence.

The reading sequence shall follow the order the artifact tree draws, depth-first, placing a parent before its children. The sequence shall hold only the artifacts the active search, filters and baseline leave in view.

A step shall stop at the first artifact and at the last artifact rather than wrap. The workspace shall disable a step control that has no destination.

The workspace shall treat the J key as a step to the next artifact. The workspace shall treat the K key as a step to the previous artifact. The workspace shall ignore both keys while the keystroke carries a modifier. The workspace shall ignore both keys while the keystroke targets a text field or an editable region. The workspace shall ignore both keys while a member edits or creates an artifact. The workspace shall ignore both keys while a dialog, a sheet or a lightbox covers the document.

On a touch screen the workspace shall treat a leftward swipe across the artifact document as a step to the next artifact. The workspace shall treat a rightward swipe as a step to the previous artifact. The workspace shall ignore a swipe that begins inside an element that scrolls horizontally. The workspace shall ignore a swipe that begins within the screen-edge strip the browser reserves for its own gestures. The swipe shall leave vertical scrolling unchanged.

The artifact tree shall expand the ancestors of the selected artifact so that its row is visible. The tree shall leave every other collapsed artifact collapsed.

artifacts.title: One reading sequence, three ways into it: controls, J / K, and a swipe
artifacts.body:
`frontend/src/utils/artifactSequence.ts` is the single answer to "what comes next". It holds the comparator and the hierarchy builder the tree itself sorts with — moved there out of `ArtifactList`, so the tree, the stepper and sibling placement cannot disagree — plus `documentOrder` (depth-first, parent before children), `sequencePosition`, `stepArtifact` and `ancestorIds`. Everything in it is pure and unit-tested. Its `buildHierarchy` also roots the members of a `parent_id` cycle rather than losing them, which the previous copy did not.

`ModuleView` builds the sequence from `filteredArtifacts`, so search, filters and the active baseline narrow what stepping walks. It is recomputed per render rather than memoized: `filteredArtifacts` is a fresh array every render, so a memo keyed on it would never hit. A step routes through the existing `handleSelectArtifact`, which writes both the store and the `?artifact=` param, so a step is the same selection a tap on the tree makes and leaves the same shareable URL.

Three entry points, one step function:

- **Controls** — `ArtifactStepper`, rendered as the first row of the artifact header card, above the title. It shows `‹ › n of m`, disables the control at each end, and hands focus to the live control when the pressed one is about to disable itself. The visible count is `aria-hidden`; a sibling `sr-only` `aria-live="polite"` region announces the artifact's ref, title and position, because a step replaces the document without moving focus.
- **Keys** — `hooks/readingKeys.ts` decides, purely, whether a keystroke is a step: J and K, no modifiers, not in a field or a contenteditable, not while editing, not while an overlay is open (`overlayIsOpen`, which the gesture shares). One `window` listener, mounted once, reading the current step through a ref, because the sequence changes identity every render.
- **Gesture** — `hooks/swipe.ts` holds the thresholds (60 px of travel, horizontal beating vertical by 1.5, within 800 ms, clear of the 24 px screen-edge strip the browser uses for back and forward) and `hooks/useSwipe.ts` the four touch handlers. Nothing is `preventDefault`-ed: React registers touch listeners passively, and judging only at `touchend` is what leaves vertical scrolling untouched. A gesture starting inside a horizontally scrolling element — a wide table, a code block — is dropped at its start, so that element keeps its own swipe.

`ArtifactList` expands the ancestors of `selectedId` so a step, a deep link or a citation never lands on a hidden row. The effect is keyed on the joined ancestor chain, so re-filtering does not re-open anything and a section closed on purpose stays closed.

Gated on the `artifact-stepping` feature key. There is no endpoint behind any of it, so the gate covers the controls only and a shared link opens everywhere.

artifacts.title: Same-site session on every deployment
artifacts.body: The system shall serve the application and its API so that the session cookie is a first-party cookie in every supported browser, including browsers that block third-party cookies outright. A deployment shall be able to place the API behind the application's own origin, and a deployment that keeps the API on a separate site shall mark the session and sign-on cookies as partitioned. A member on a phone or tablet browser shall be able to sign in and stay signed in for the session lifetime.

artifacts.title: Layout by screen width
artifacts.body: The application shall select its layout from the width of the screen. The application shall use a phone layout at 640 pixels and below and a narrow tablet layout at 900 pixels and below. On a phone the application shall present the project navigation as a drawer opened from a button in the header. On a touch device the application shall treat the auto-hiding panel state as hidden. Every edge strip that recovers a panel shall be at least 44 pixels wide. No view shall scroll the page horizontally at 360 pixels wide. Content that does not fit a region shall scroll within that region, and the application shall not clip it. The application shall size itself to the visible viewport, so that a browser toolbar never covers a bottom control. The application shall respect the device's safe-area insets.

artifacts.title: Stacked requirements workspace on narrow screens
artifacts.body: Below the tablet breakpoint the requirements workspace shall present its tree, document and notes as one region at a time, switched by a control that stays visible, each scrolling within its own bounds, so that the workspace still fits the window without clipping any of the three. Selecting an artifact in the tree shall switch to the document. The guided definition wizard shall present its step rail as a progress bar and its assistant as a sheet that opens over the step on the same widths.

artifacts.title: Touch alternatives for every drag, hover and right-click action
artifacts.body: Every action the application offers through a drag, a hover or a right-click shall also be reachable through a tap. Each artifact row shall carry a menu button that opens the same actions as its context menu. A member shall be able to move an artifact to a chosen parent and position through a dialog, and the dialog shall apply the same placement rules as a drag. Figure actions shall be visible without hover on a touch device. Drag on the tree and the board shall use pointer events so that a finger can drag where the screen allows it.

artifacts.title: Tap targets, text size and fit on a phone
artifacts.body: Every primary control shall present a tap target of at least 44 by 44 pixels on a touch device. Every other button shall present a tap target of at least 36 pixels high on a touch device. Every text input, text area and select shall render at a font size of at least 16 pixels, so that a phone browser does not zoom on focus. The system shall render no visible text smaller than 12 pixels. At a viewport width of 390 pixels the system shall show every control of a dialog, a menu and a settings page inside the viewport. At that width the system shall clip no such control. Sign-in fields shall carry the autocomplete hints a password manager needs. Chat composers shall carry a send key hint. Every table shall scroll horizontally within its own container. No dialog shall be wider than the viewport.

artifacts.title: Review and approval from a phone
artifacts.body: On a phone the review queue and the proposal list shall present each item as a card carrying its title, reference, the change it proposes and approve, reject and open actions, with the proposed change readable at 360 pixels wide. The notifications bell shall open a full-screen list whose entries lead to the mobile view of what they concern. Artifact comments and the V&V Assistant shall use the same single-column chat layout as the public interview page.

artifacts.title: Board actions without drag
artifacts.body: On a phone the board shall show one column at a time with a control to move between columns. Each card shall offer an action sheet with move to a chosen column, assign to a person or agent, and open, so that every board transition, including handing a card to an agent, is available without a drag.

artifacts.title: Runner control from a phone
artifacts.body: A member shall be able to lease, extend and end a cloud runner from a phone, and shall be able to complete a relayed vendor sign-in on it: the sign-in link shall open in the phone's browser, and the field that takes the returned code or address shall accept a paste from a password manager and submit with the keyboard's send key. A member shall be able to launch, watch, retry and cancel a run from a phone.

artifacts.title: Installable application and push notifications
artifacts.body: The application shall remain installable as a standalone web application on phones and tablets, shall declare screenshots and shortcuts to the review queue, the board and notifications, and shall keep serving live content without caching a shell. When a member opts in on a device, the system shall deliver the high-signal notification types to that device by web push, shall store one subscription per device, and shall let the member withdraw the subscription.

artifacts.title: Mobile test coverage
artifacts.body: The end-to-end suite shall run the smoke journey on a WebKit engine and on a phone and a tablet device profile in addition to desktop Chrome, and shall run a mobile journey covering sign-in, approving a review item, moving a board card through its action sheet, and reaching the cloud runner sign-in screen. A viewport check shall fail the suite when any view scrolls horizontally at 360 pixels wide.

artifacts.title: Mobile support plan 2026-09-07
artifacts.body:
# Mobile support plan

Status: approved and implemented through Phase 3, 2026-09-07 — see
section 8 for what shipped and what is deferred. Evidence base: the frontend
readiness review in `docs/assessments/2026-09-07-mobile-readiness.md`.
Requirements recorded in the OpenV Platform project under **Mobile**
(NEED-13, REQ-101 … REQ-110, DES-23, TC-50).

## 1. Where we are

OpenV's frontend is a desktop application. The facts that matter:

- **iOS cannot sign in to production.** The frontend and API live on two
  different `up.railway.app` hosts, which browsers treat as different *sites*
  (the suffix is on the Public Suffix List), so the session cookie is a
  third-party cookie (`SameSite=None`). Safari drops third-party cookies
  outright, and every browser on iOS is Safari underneath. Sign-in appears to
  succeed, the next request answers 401, and the app bounces back to the
  login page. Android Chrome still works but is on the same road. Self-hosted
  deployments on one domain are unaffected.
- **No responsive layer.** Six media queries in the whole codebase, all in
  leaf components (lightbox, gallery, project cards, help panel); no
  component knows the screen width; styling is inline pixel widths. The
  requirements workspace needs about 460 px before the document pane has any
  width at all, and the guided wizard needs 852 px with no wrapping. Both
  clip overflow rather than scroll, by design (REQ-53 fits the window).
- **No touch layer.** Every drag is HTML5 drag-and-drop, which touch
  browsers do not synthesise: reparenting an artifact and launching an agent
  from the board are drag-only. Seven artifact actions live behind a
  right-click menu. Figure actions appear on hover. Panels in auto-hide mode
  open on hover and are recovered through a 10 px edge strip.
- **Input details bite:** every field is 14 px, so iOS zooms on focus and
  stays zoomed; the login card is a fixed 380 px and overflows an iPhone SE;
  `100vh` is used where `100dvh` is needed, so bottom bars sit under the
  Safari toolbar.
- **What already works:** the app is installable (manifest with maskable
  icons, `display: standalone`, a deliberately non-caching service worker);
  routes are code-split so the heavy grid and graph libraries stay off the
  first load; the public interview chat is a genuine phone-first screen and
  works on iOS because it uses no cookie; the crew graph (Cytoscape) already
  handles touch; the design tokens support dark mode and system preference.

## 2. Who needs mobile, for what

| Persona | Jobs on a phone or tablet | Today |
|---|---|---|
| PER-4 External stakeholder | Answer an interview from a link | Works |
| PER-1 Solo founder, PER-2 Company admin | Approve or reject proposals and reviews; read a requirement someone linked; reply to a comment or ask the V&V Assistant; see a run fail and retry it; act on a budget alert; start a cloud runner and sign an agent in from the browser relay | Blocked on iOS; unusable layout elsewhere |
| PER-3 Team contributor | Move a board card, comment on it, hand work to an agent; read requirements on a tablet in a meeting or on the shop floor | Same |

Not mobile jobs, and explicitly out of scope: authoring long documents,
building crews, editing the traceability matrix, resizing columns, installing
the Agent Connector.

The transient runner with browser-relayed sign-in (REQ-57, REQ-58) is the
feature that makes a phone genuinely useful: a founder can lease a runner,
sign Claude in by pasting a code, and launch agents from anywhere with
nothing installed. The plan protects that path first.

## 3. Strategy: one responsive web app, installed as a PWA

Recommendation: make the existing React app responsive and touch-capable and
ship it through the PWA shell that already exists. Not a native app, not a
wrapper.

- The product is a live collaborative tool with no offline requirement; the
  service worker's no-cache stance stays.
- One codebase, one deployment, no store review, and every fix ships through
  the existing promote-to-release path.
- Web Push reaches installed PWAs on iOS 16.4 and later and on Android, so
  notifications do not require a native app.
- A Capacitor wrapper can be added later without redoing any of this work if
  store presence or native share sheets ever matter.

## 4. Phases

### Phase 0 — Unblock iOS (one PR, the prerequisite for everything else)

Serve the API and the app from **one origin**. Two ways; the first is
recommended because it needs no DNS and removes cross-site cookies entirely:

- **A. Proxy the API through the frontend's nginx.** Add
  `location /api/ { proxy_pass http://openv.railway.internal:8080; }` (the
  API's Railway private domain) with `proxy_buffering off` and
  `proxy_read_timeout` raised for SSE, `client_max_body_size 32m` to match
  the API's body cap, and forwarded headers. Build the frontend with
  `REACT_APP_API_URL` empty and make the client default to a relative
